translation.globalBar.modelBucketInfo: Selects the weights for this component. Different quantizations trade memory use for precision. Incompatible files cannot be selected.
translation.globalBar.yue2SheetTranscriberInfo: Writes the ABC score a YuE2 cover follows. SheetSage2-Refined (anime-song) reads odd meters, slash chords and tension chords that SheetSage2 writes as 4/4 and plain triads. It needs SheetSage2 installed too: it reuses its encoder.

translation.trainingStudio.review.empty: Nothing waiting. Runs appear here once they have a saved checkpoint pair.

translation.trainingStudio.mm3.previewEnabledInfo: Pauses the trainer to render checkpoint samples, then resumes it. Turn off to set both preview cadences to zero.
translation.trainingStudio.ace.noCheckpointPreviews: ACE does not support automatic checkpoint previews. Use Audition below to compare LM adapters and saved milestones.
translation.trainingStudio.ace.datasetChanged: Dataset changed while the recipe was resolved. Review the form and start again.

translation.trainingStudio.sa3.scope: Instrumental adapters only. Batch size 1; the base model, SAME audio encoder and T5Gemma text encoder stay frozen.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preparation: Preparation strips vocals with SuperSep level 5, then converts derived audio to 44.1 kHz stereo. Originals stay intact. Captions include genre, BPM, key and time signature; lyrics are omitted.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.enginePause: Preparation runs first, then generation pauses while the trainer owns the GPU. The engine restarts after completion, failure or cancellation.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.unavailable: Not ready · {{backend}}. Training requires CUDA or CPU, ace-train and all required models.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.missing: Missing models: {{files}}. Install them in Model Manager.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.runInfo: Start a new run or resume a saved checkpoint with its original prepared audio and recipe. Only the total step target can increase on resume.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.adapterNameInfo: Use letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. Each run gets a separate dated folder.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.auditionInfo: Use a held-out instrumental prompt. Render with the adapter on, then switch it off and render again with the same seed and duration. Results are saved in the library.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.localAudition: Auditions use this PC. Worker exports are listed below; copy the published GGUF to this PC’s models/sa3-adapters folder and select This PC to audition it.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.adapterInfo: Choose a validated inference export from this PC’s SA3 adapter catalogue. Raw trainer weights and optimizer state are not inference adapters.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.noAdapters: No published adapters on this PC
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.useAdapterInfo: Off renders the base model at strength 0. On applies the selected adapter at the strength below.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.caption: Held-out caption
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.captionInfo: Describe instrumental music that was not used for training. Keep this caption unchanged when comparing the base and adapter.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.strengthInfo: 0 uses the base model, 1 applies the full adapter. Higher values can exaggerate the style.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.auditionSeedInfo: Keep the same seed for both sides of a comparison. This audition uses 8 steps and MD Pingpong Blend with no post-processing.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.auditionSecondsInfo: Output duration, from 1 to 384 seconds. Keep it fixed for both sides of a comparison.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.fields.stepsInfo: Total optimizer step target. The pilot recipe is 1,000 steps. On resume this is the total target, not the number of additional steps.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.fields.rankInfo: Adapter capacity. The initial recipe uses 16; increasing it trains more parameters and uses more memory.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.fields.alphaInfo: Training scale for the low-rank update. The initial recipe pairs rank 16 with alpha 16. This stays fixed on resume.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.fields.learningRateIn: Size of each optimizer update. The initial recipe uses 0.0001. Larger updates can become unstable.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.fields.durationInfo: Maximum training crop, from 1 to 384 seconds. Shorter crops reduce memory use. The server default is 380 seconds; measured memory and speed depend on your hardware.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.fields.seedInfo: Controls training randomness. Saved with the recipe and preserved on resume.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.fields.checkpointEver: Save resumable optimizer state every this many steps. Cancelling during model loading may leave no checkpoint.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.fields.exportEveryInf: Write inference snapshots in the run folder every this many steps. 0 disables periodic snapshots. A completed run publishes its validated final adapter to the picker.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preview.title: Checkpoint previews (optional)
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preview.enableInfo: Each cadence step saves an inference snapshot and renders every prompt and seed below, one at a time, after the trainer exits and before it resumes. Off: no snapshots or previews.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preview.resumeKeeps: A resumed run keeps the preview settings it started with.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preview.everyStepsInf: Render previews every this many training steps. Starts from the recipe snapshot interval.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preview.secondsInfo: Length of each rendered preview, from 1 to 384 seconds. Longer previews take longer at every checkpoint.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preview.seedsInfo: Up to four whole-number seeds, separated by commas. Every checkpoint renders each prompt with each seed, so checkpoints compare like for like.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preview.promptsInfo: One prompt per line. Use instrumental descriptions that were not in the training captions, and keep them the same for the whole run.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preview.needPrompt: Add at least one prompt, or turn previews off.
translation.trainingStudio.sa3.preview.none: No previews for this run yet.

translation.trainingStudio.assets.sa3EncodedOn: The trainer’s encoding cache matches the prepared audio and captions ({{count}} clips).
translation.trainingStudio.assets.sa3EncodedOff: No valid encoding cache. Training encodes the audio and captions.
translation.trainingStudio.assets.sa3SnapshotsOn: {{count}} inference snapshots saved from training runs.

translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.prepareInfo: Build the dataset first. Preparation encodes audio into eight HeartMuLa codebooks and checks tags, lyrics and the model context limit. Changed samples must be prepared again before training.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.forceInfo: Re-encode every sample, including valid cached samples. Leave off to reuse unchanged preparation.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.reviewInfo: Compare the base model, saved checkpoints and final adapter with the same tags, lyrics, seed and sampler. Training pauses while each preview renders.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.takeDetails: up to {{seconds}} s · seed {{seed}} · temperature {{temperature}} · top-k {{topk}} · CFG {{cfg}} · codec {{codecSteps}} / {{codecGuidance}}
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.resumeInfo: Continue a saved run with its recipe, preview settings and optimizer state. Recipe edits apply only to a new run.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.adapterNameInfo: Name for the saved adapter. Use letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens, up to 64 characters.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.enablePreviews: Render a full-song preview at every checkpoint
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.enablePreviewsI: The server pauses training, renders one full song from the dataset, then resumes. The base model is rendered first and the final adapter last. Keep previews enabled to hear how the adapter changes.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.previewEveryInf: Steps between audible previews. More frequent previews add more pauses.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.previewSecondsI: The longest a preview may run, from 5 to 240 seconds. A full song ends on its own before that. Longer previews pause training for longer at every checkpoint.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.previewSeedInfo: The random seed used for every preview render, so previews across checkpoints are directly comparable rather than each landing on a different random take.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.previewLyricsIn: Lyric Studio generation: the newest lyrics generated for this dataset's artist in Lyric Studio, so each checkpoint sings a song it never trained on. Falls back to the dataset's lyrics when there are none. Dataset lyrics: the first sung track's own lyrics. Either way the tags come from the dataset, because that is what training saw, and every checkpoint of a run uses the same words.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.previewLyricsGe: Lyric Studio generation (falls back to dataset lyrics)
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.previewSongHint: The tags come from the first sung track in this dataset. Tags and lyrics overrides below replace either choice.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.previewTagsInfo: Replaces the preview track's own tags for the rendered sample. Leave blank to use the track's tags as-is.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.previewLyricsOv: Replaces the preview track's own lyrics for the rendered sample. Leave blank to use the track's lyrics as-is.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.resumeSummary: Resume {{run}} with its saved recipe and preview settings.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.prepareRequired: Prepare a non-empty dataset with no stale samples before training.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.field.stepsInfo: Number of optimizer updates. More steps take longer and can overfit the dataset.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.field.rankInfo: Adapter capacity. Higher ranks use more memory. The starting recipe uses rank 64.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.field.alphaInfo: Adapter scaling relative to rank. The starting recipe pairs alpha 64 with rank 64.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.field.learningR: Size of each weight update. Larger values learn faster but can make training unstable.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.field.gradAccum: Micro-batches per optimizer update. Higher values do more work per step without increasing the micro-batch size.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.field.seedInfo: Seed for training randomness. Keep it fixed when comparing recipes.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.field.loraDropo: Randomly drops adapter inputs while training, which can reduce overfitting on a small dataset. 0 is off; 0.05 is a proven value that adds about 8% to each step and 1.3 GiB of memory.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.field.checkpoin: Save resumable state every this many steps. Zero saves only when stopping or finishing. Preview cadence is separate.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.presetStorageEr: Could not save presets in this browser.

translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.batchInfo: Choose datasets, then apply the recipe below to each in order. The queue survives closing the page and server restarts.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.chainInfo: Prepares missing or stale HeartMuLa audio, then trains with the settings below. Unchanged prepared audio is reused.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.resumePathInfo: Paste the ID or folder of a resumable run belonging to this dataset. Its saved recipe is restored.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.resumeInvalid: Choose a resumable run from this dataset.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.presetInfo: Presets change the update budget and songs per update. Balanced uses the current 480 by 4 recipe. Fast halves the updates; Thorough uses 720 updates averaging eight songs. HOT-Approved uses the current server recipe.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.userPresetInfo: Save and share recipe settings. Presets never include dataset, adapter name or resume paths.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.baseInfo: HeartMuLa training uses the 3B F16 backbone.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.gpuInfo: The current HeartMuLa trainer selects its CUDA device automatically. Per-run GPU selection is not supported.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.adapterTypeInfo: The current HeartMuLa trainer supports backbone LoRA adapters.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.adapterFolder: Adapters are saved in your global adapters folder under heartmula-lm-adapters/.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.clearCachesInfo: Clears only this dataset's prepared HeartMuLa audio. YuE2, ACE and MM3 caches, source files, labels and adapters are kept.
translation.trainingStudio.heartmula.allPrepare: Runs the preparation stage below. Training is on the Train page.
translation.api.error.sessionExpired: Your session expired — signing you back in
translation.api.error.notFound: That item no longer exists on the server
translation.api.error.serverError: The server ran into a problem
translation.noModels.message: No models installed yet. Download one in the Model Manager and the engine starts by itself.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.ladderHint: A take marked preview_limit was cut at the length limit mid-song, so its abrupt end is the limit, not the planner. Renders are not deterministic: two tracks per rung is the minimum to trust a rung. Render adds more tracks to a rung with the count and length above.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.reviewCompleteInfo: You have found the winner and will not score the other rungs. The Review tab then counts this ladder as scored and offers it to Finish scored, which uses the best-scored rung.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.discardOnWorker: Discard on {{worker}} — no rung from this ladder, free its checkpoints and previews there too
translation.trainingStudio.refine.ladderInfo: A refinement run and its rungs. Rung cards carry the planner's KL and the decoder's reconstruction at that checkpoint, the rendered tracks, and your scores.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.secondsInfo: Preview length. A take shorter than the planned song is cut mid-song at this limit and has no ending, which can read as corruption in its last seconds; the take then shows "preview_limit". Keep it long enough for a whole song (most albums fit in 300 s; 360 is the most).
translation.trainingStudio.refine.takesInfo: Tracks per rung, different seeds. Renders are not deterministic: one take can decay late while another from the same checkpoint is clean, so two is the minimum to trust a rung.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.draftInfo: Previews only: the decoder runs 12 ODE steps instead of 32, with the velocity cache off (a raised cache ratio blunts artist likeness), about a third of the decoder time. Timbre is a little softer; structure, diction and late-song behaviour, which the planner sets, are unchanged. Off renders previews at production quality.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.parallelInfo: Render while training continues instead of pausing it at each rung. Needs the VRAM for both (about 22 GB measured); renders run at about half speed and training a little slower. Untick on a smaller card.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.autoPreviewInfo: Render the tracks for every rung as it lands, so the ladder is ready to listen to when the run ends. Off: render rungs by hand from the ladder.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narKneeToggleInfo: Stop once a line fitted through the last 10 checkpoints (100 steps) gains under 0.5%: a real plateau, not one noisy reading. Off: train to the step budget or the recon target.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narKeepDeltaInfo: During further decoder training a checkpoint is kept only when the reconstruction meter has dropped by at least this since the last kept one; the rest are deleted so the ladder shows real progress, not every 10 steps. The newest checkpoint is always kept.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narKeepDelta: Keep a checkpoint per recon drop
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narLrInfo: Fraction of the source run's rate for the decoder pass, on top of the same pacing the ladder used (its 30-step warm-up and any halving from skipped rungs). 0.1 is the ladder's own value; 0.2 is twice that. The plain run rate (1) threw a converged decoder out of its basin within six steps, so raise this in small steps and watch the reconstruction meter over the first checkpoints.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narBudgetInfo: The most decoder steps to train after the pick. At about 1.5 s a step, 250 is roughly 6 minutes.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narTargetInfo: Stop the decoder once its reconstruction error (how closely it reproduces the album's own latents on fixed probes; lower is better, typically 0.29–0.35 and falling) reaches this value. Some albums plateau above it; the knee rule and the step budget then stop the run instead.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narFurtherInfo: When you press "Use this rung", the decoder trains on from that rung with the planner frozen, until the reconstruction target, the step budget, or the point where the reconstruction meter stops improving, whichever comes first. That final checkpoint becomes the adapter. Off: the rung is used as it is.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.secDecoder: Decoder, after you pick a rung
translation.trainingStudio.refine.lrInfo: Fraction of the source run's rate. A converged adapter restarted at full rate diverged in three steps, so refinement walks: the rate ramps up over the first 30 steps and halves itself whenever the KL jumps more than one rung between checkpoints. Lower if rungs are still being skipped.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.rungInfo: A checkpoint is saved, and previews rendered, each time the KL reading crosses the next multiple of this. Smaller rungs give a finer ladder and more previews to listen to.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.ceilingInfo: The planner stops when its KL to the base model reaches this. Late-song decay has shown from about 1.7 on some albums and not at all by 1.8 on others, so the ceiling is a search range, not a target: pick the last good rung by ear.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.sourceInfo: The run to continue from. Its last checkpoint is the starting point: the planner is unfrozen there and both halves train on. Refinements of refinements are fine; the run list shows what each one reached.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.intro: The safe presets stop the planner at a conservative KL. Some artists take more. This continues a finished run with the planner live and the decoder along for the ride, saves a checkpoint at every KL rung up to the ceiling, and renders a preview per rung so you can hear where it starts to fall apart late in the song. Pick the last good rung.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.title: Refine the planner
translation.trainingStudio.refine.noticePlannerDone: Refinement finished. Listen to the rungs, then press Use this rung on the one you choose. With Further training for NAR on, the decoder then trains on from that rung and the adapter is linked when it stops; off, the rung is linked as it is and you can clean up.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.noticeDecoderDone: Decoder training finished. Press Use this rung on its last checkpoint to link the adapter and clean up.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narNoCheckpoint: The decoder run left no complete checkpoint.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narStarted: Decoder training on from step {{step}}; the adapter is linked when it stops.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.narRemoteUnsupport: NAR further training on a ladder trained on {{worker}} is not supported yet. Turn off Further training for NAR to finish this rung directly, or pick a different rung.
translation.trainingStudio.refine.deleteConfirm: Delete this run and its {{n}} checkpoint(s) from disk? Scores you entered are kept.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.resumeStateNote: The optimizer state is deleted when a run exports cleanly — it is the run's middle, not its result. A run that stops early keeps it, and the engine will only continue from it if the rank, alpha, trained sites, trigger, seed and grad-accum all match, on this same machine and build.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.tSamplingInfo: Which denoising timesteps get sampled during training. logit-normal biases sampling toward the middle of the noise range; uniform samples every timestep equally.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.logEveryInfo: How often, in steps, the trainer writes a log line with its metrics. Only affects how closely you can watch progress, not the training itself.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.clipBlockHint: How many steps one working set of clips is held for before the next block is drawn. With per-clip codec ids every clip is its own conditioning, so drawing from the whole album misses the K/V cache almost every step and re-runs the AR prefix. Raising it reuses the cache longer per block; 0 draws from everything.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.kvCacheHint: How many AR-prefix caches are held at once, about 104 MB each at 10 s clips. A real VRAM knob: raising it uses more VRAM but can reuse more cached prefixes; 8 is what was measured.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.abcDropoutHint: Chance a clip whose source has a lead sheet trains cot=off instead of cot=full this draw. A source with no lead sheet always trains cot=off. 0.5 is upstream's own split; raising it trains more like a source with no lead sheet, lowering it leans more on cot=full.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionDropoutHint: Chance of swapping in the EMPTY style prefix instead of the real caption on a given step. 0 is not "more likeness": it is the trigger word ceasing to mean anything relative to no trigger word. Raising it trains the trigger to matter more; too high leaves too little signal from the real captions.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.seedInfo: Seeds the random draws that choose clip order and dropout during training. Changing it changes which clips and dropout draws land on which step, not the training recipe itself; the same seed with the same recipe reproduces the same run.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.weightDecayInfo: Shrinks the adapter's weights a little on every step, independent of the loss. Higher discourages large weights, which can reduce overfitting but also blunt the adapter's learned effect; 0 turns it off.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.maxGradNormInfo: Caps how large the gradient is allowed to get on any one step, cutting it back to this length if it is bigger. Guards against a spike destabilising the run; too low a cap can slow learning by blunting every real update as well.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.gradAccumInfo: How many steps of gradients get summed before the optimizer applies an update, which behaves like a larger batch without the extra VRAM. Raising it smooths updates but makes each optimizer step rarer; 1 updates every step.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.warmupInfo: How many steps the learning rate ramps up from zero at the start of the run, before the schedule above takes over. More warmup steps ease into training more gently; fewer reach the full rate sooner but risk an unstable start.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.lrSchedulerInfo: How the learning rate moves over the run. cosine decays it from the starting rate down toward zero as training progresses; constant holds it steady for the whole run.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.lrInfo: How big a step the optimizer takes on each update. Higher trains faster but risks instability; lower is steadier but slower to converge. Only used when the optimizer above is not Prodigy, which sets its own effective rate automatically.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.alphaInfo: Scales how strongly the LoRA weights apply relative to the rank. Raising it makes the adapter's effect stronger at the same rank; lowering it weakens it.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.costHint: Measured on one card: 17.0 GB at rank 128 and 19.6 GB at rank 256, the roughly 7 GB bf16 base included in both. {{clips}} clips in the cache; 10,000 steps at rank 256 took about 12 minutes.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.baseHint: Which YuE2 LM checkpoint the LoRA trains against; the same base must be loaded at generation time for the adapter to apply. Only bf16 has been trained on here. Whether a quantized base trains usefully at all is not established, so the others are offered without a ranking.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.targetAttnMlpHint: Attention plus the FFN on all 28 NAR blocks — what the measured runs used.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.targetHint: Which weights inside the NAR half the LoRA touches. nar_attn trains only attention; nar_attn_mlp adds the feed-forward layers on all 28 NAR blocks — 196 sites — and is what the measured runs used; nar_attn_mlp_proj adds the projection layers on top of that. Training more sites gives the adapter more places to change the sound, at the cost of a larger file and more VRAM.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.saveEveryHint: How often, in steps, a checkpoint snapshot is written to disk. These are the rungs on the ladder — and where a killed run comes back from. Lower means more frequent snapshots to pick from, at the cost of more disk writes.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.rankHint: How much capacity the LoRA has. 256 is what was measured; 128 saves about 2.6 GB of VRAM at the cost of some capacity, and the ladder between them, plus upstream's default of 16, have not been heard here. Higher rank can capture more detail but costs more VRAM and a larger adapter file.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.stepsInfo: How many training steps to run. Step count is the only lever measured for this trainer, so it is the only thing the Recipe presets move. More steps mean more training time and, past a point, a risk of overcooking the adapter; fewer steps finish faster but may undertrain.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.triggerInfo: Put in front of every training caption, and the only handle the trained style has at generation time. Required: without one the adapter has no word to address it by, and the run is refused rather than warned about twelve minutes in.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.presetInfo: Step count is the only lever measured here, so it is the only thing the presets move. At the measured 0.065 s per step the wall clock is close to linear: 10,000 steps is about 12 minutes and 20,000 about 23.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.needsLatents: Encode the latents first — training reads the cache, not the audio.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.trainBlurb: Trains a LoRA on the frozen NAR half of the YuE2 LM from the cached latents. Snapshots are written as plain safetensors files you can load straight into the YuE2 adapter field — there is no install step. The engine is paused for the run.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.peakOver: about {{gb}} GB, more than your {{totalGb}} GB — lower the rank
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.peakTight: about {{gb}} GB of your {{totalGb}} GB — fits with nothing left for the desktop
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.runsHalted: This run still holds its optimizer state, which means it stopped before its clean finish — the engine deletes that file on export. Continuing a run is not wired up yet; start a fresh one with the same recipe.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.runsBlurb: Every NAR LoRA this dataset has produced. Each snapshot is a plain safetensors file, so the whole ladder is loadable — copy a path into the YuE2 adapter field to hear that rung.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.enginePaused: The engine is paused while this runs and restarted afterwards.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.ppReCut: The cache was cut at {{have}} frames and this form says {{want}}. The manifest will be rewritten — no audio is re-encoded.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.forceHint: On by default: re-running rewrites the manifest with the caption mode chosen above (otherwise an old cut keeps its old captions) and re-cuts at the clip length. Cached latents are clip-length independent, so this costs no GPU time.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.limitInfo: Caps how many files this run encodes, useful for a quick test before committing to the whole dataset. 0 encodes every scanned file.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.onlyHint: Only encodes files whose name contains this text, case-insensitive. Blank encodes every file the scan finds.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.haloHint: Extra frames of context added to each side of an encoder tile so neighbouring tiles blend without a seam. The floor is the encoder's own receptive field; the engine refuses anything less.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.tileFramesInfo: How many frames of audio the VAE encoder processes in one pass while cutting the cache.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.ackSidecarHint: The run is refused without this. Tick it only if training the style encoder on "caption:"/"genre:" field syntax and full lyrics is what you meant.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.ackSidecar: Train on the ACE sidecars as they are
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.defaultCaptionInfo: The exact text used as the style prompt on every training clip, with the trigger word placed in front of it. There is no per-track variation in this mode.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.decodeNoFfmpegInfo: Which decoder reads the source audio before encoding. No ffmpeg in this install, so only WAV and MP3 can be decoded either way.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.decodeInfo: Which decoder reads the source audio before encoding. auto uses the built-in WAV/MP3 decoder and falls back to ffmpeg for everything else; forcing ffmpeg puts one resampler across the whole corpus instead of mixing two.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionStaleCache: {{n}} tracks have a .yue2.txt planner caption, but this cache was cut with "{{mode}}" and trained on the ACE captions instead. Run the cache again with the caption mode above to use them (a manifest rewrite; nothing is re-encoded).
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.loudnessStaleCache: This cache was cut before loudness normalization, so it trains at each album's mastering level (loud albums then render clipped). Run the cache again: every track is brought to -14 LUFS and re-encoded.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionFoundIgnored: {{n}} of the scanned tracks ship a sidecar with lyrics and this mode throws them away. The cursor-span stage and the AR half both need them.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionFound: {{n}} of the scanned tracks ship a sidecar with lyrics, and this mode reads them.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionTxtHintShort: The ACE sidecar fed in raw and whole, "caption:"/"genre:" syntax included.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionTxt: The raw sidecar file, field names and all
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionDefaultHintSh: The same style text on every clip, trigger word in front.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionDefault: One caption I type here, on every clip
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionNoneHintShort: NAR-only: later stages skip every track without lyrics.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionNone: Nothing: the trigger word is the whole style
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionYue2HintShort: Default. Same lyrics as the sidecar mode, but the style sentence is the planner caption.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionYue2: Sidecar lyrics, with the one-sentence YuE2 caption (.yue2.txt) as the style
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionAceHintShort: Carries the caption and lyrics through; the only mode besides yue2 the later stages can use.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionAce: Read the sidecars: caption and lyrics
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.captionModeInfo: What text the trainer uses as the style prompt on each clip. The sidecar modes ("Read the sidecars" and the YuE2-caption one) are the only ones that also carry the lyrics through, which the cursor-span stage and the AR half both need — anything else and those stages skip every track. "Nothing" leaves only the trigger word as the style, "One caption I type here" repeats the same sentence on every clip, and "The raw sidecar file" feeds the whole ACE sidecar in verbatim, field names included.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.clipSecondsInfo: How many seconds of audio each training clip covers once cut from the cache. The trainer takes the clip length from this cache, so changing it here rewrites the manifest next time you encode. At 25 frames per second, 10 s is 250 frames, which is what every measured run used. Raising it gives the model more context per clip at the cost of slower encoding and training; lowering it is cheaper but each clip carries less.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.ppNoFfmpeg: {{n}} of the {{total}} files are FLAC/OGG/M4A and need ffmpeg to decode, which this install does not have. They would all be skipped, so the run is refused.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.ppFlatScan: This stage scans the source folder FLAT. Subfolders are not searched whatever the dataset's recursive setting says, and rows excluded in the dataset are still encoded — the engine takes a folder, not the dataset manifest.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.ppCache: Cached: {{clips}} clip(s) of {{frames}} frames from {{sources}} track(s).
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.ppScan: {{files}} audio file(s) directly in the source folder; the dataset has {{samples}} sample(s){{excluded}}.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.ppBlurb: Encodes the dataset's audio through the YuE2 VAE once and caches the latents, which is what the NAR trainer reads — it never sees the audio. About 4 minutes for a 12 to 15 track album, and a 12-track album comes out at roughly 240 clips. Re-running is cheap: anything already encoded is reused.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.ppCost: About {{gb}} GB of VRAM: the VAE encoder plus a 3.7 GB compute buffer.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.enginePaused: The engine is paused while this runs and restarted afterwards.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.allowNoTriggerHint: The adapter then has no word that addresses it, and it is the caption dropout's counterpart — there is nothing left for the empty-caption draws to teach.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.allowOvertrainHint: Past there upstream says the model stops learning the style and starts memorising the songs. The settled recipe is {{n}} steps.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.cursorBlocked: The cursor loss is on but no source has cursor spans, and the engine refuses that rather than print "cursor nan" for the whole run. Run the align stage above, or set the cursor weight to 0.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sidecarsHint: The manifest carries no lyrics, so with this off the prefix falls back to the two fields above — and a style-less, lyric-less prefix trains happily and is wrong.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.lyricsHint: Same, for the lyrics half of the prefix.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.styleHint: Used only for a source with no sidecar caption.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.logEveryHint: How often, in steps, a training-loss line is written to the log. It only changes how often progress is reported, not the run itself.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.evalEveryHint: Held-out loss on the regulariser pack. 0 turns it off.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.ckptFromHint: The step the first snapshot is saved at; after that, snapshots follow the "Snapshot every" interval above. Raising it skips saving the earliest, least-trained rungs of the ladder.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.attnHint: Which attention kernel trains with. Flash drops the retained softmax — several GB at full song length — and errors out on a backend that cannot do it. The recipe was proven on exact.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.chunkHint: How many tokens the cross-entropy loss is computed over at once. Lower values use less VRAM for the loss computation at the cost of more passes; it does not change what is learned, only how the loss is computed.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.maxLenHint: Tokens. A longer song truncates without its end marker, so it never teaches a fake ending. This also sizes the per-layer buffers — it is the VRAM lever.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.adamBeta2Hint: Upstream's, not the LM optimizer's 0.999. It is how long the second moment remembers, which sets how hard a small corpus is memorised.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.adamBeta1Hint: How much the optimizer smooths the gradient direction across steps. Higher values smooth more, which steadies noisy updates; lower values react to each step's gradient more directly.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.seedHint: Fixes the random draws (artist/minted mix, dropout, shuffling) so the same recipe reproduces the same run. Changing it gives a different draw order, not a different recipe.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.weightDecayHint: Shrinks the LoRA weights a little on every step, independent of the loss. Raising it pulls the adapter toward doing less, which resists overfitting a small corpus; 0 turns it off.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.maxGradNormHint: Caps the size of each gradient update before it is applied. Lower values clamp harder, which resists a single bad batch derailing the run; too low can slow learning down.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.gradAccumHint: How many micro-steps of gradients are summed before the weights actually update. Raising it simulates a bigger batch on the same VRAM at the cost of more time per logged step; 1 updates on every micro-step.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.warmupHint: Steps at the start of the run where the learning rate ramps up from zero instead of starting at full strength. More steps ramp up more gradually; 0 starts the run at full learning rate immediately.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.schedStepsHint: Not the run length. Moving the steps without moving this changes where on the curve the run stops.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.lrSchedulerHint: How the learning rate moves over the cosine horizon below. cosine decays it across that horizon; constant holds it flat at the learning rate for the whole run.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.alphaHint: Scales how strongly the LoRA's learned change is applied on top of the base weights, independent of rank. Raising it strengthens the adapter's pull at the same rank; lowering it weakens it.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.lrHint: Cosine over a {{h}}-step horizon that a {{n}}-step run never reaches the end of — the run is the head of that curve, not a complete decay.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.baseHint: Which AR base checkpoint the LoRA trains against. Only bf16 has been trained on here (marked "measured"). Whether a quantized base trains usefully at all is not established, so the others are offered without a ranking.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.styleTemplateHint: How the prompt is built from the trigger and the caption. Generation has to compose the same string, which is why it is stamped into the adapter — changing this after training makes the trigger mean something different than what the adapter learned.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.abcDropoutNone: No source has a lead sheet yet — run the lead-sheet stage, or leave this at any value; every source trains cot=off either way.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.abcDropoutHint: Chance a source with a lead sheet trains cot=off instead of cot=full this draw. 0.5 is upstream's own split.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.cursorWeightNone: No source has cursor spans yet — run the align stage, or set this to 0.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.cursorWeightHint: The lyric-timing loss. 0 turns it off.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.artistFracHint: One draw per micro-step: artist song or minted song. 0.5 is the measured mix.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.artistFracNoMinted: Without the regulariser pack every draw is an artist song whatever this says.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.captionDropoutHint: Chance of dropping the caption and training on the trigger alone. 0 is not "more likeness": it is the trigger ceasing to mean anything on its own.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.targetHint: Which weights inside the AR model the LoRA touches. attn is the attention projections only; attn_mlp is qkvo plus gate/up/down on all 28 AR layers — upstream's own group, and what the recipe was proven with. More sites means more trainable parameters and a heavier adapter.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.saveEveryHint: Rungs on the ladder. The rung is picked by ear afterwards, so a coarse ladder is a smaller choice.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.rankHint: Defaults to 128. Below 64 the gradient probes come back inconclusive.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.stepsHint: {{n}} is the settled recipe, with the ear picking a rung around {{pick}}. Nothing has been timed here, so there is no clock estimate to give you.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.triggerMissing: Required. Without one the trained style has no handle at generation time, and the engine only warns — a silent warning inside a long run is not a warning.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.triggerHint: Goes in front of every training caption and is stamped into the adapter, so half a run under a different one is a different adapter.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.trainNeedsLatents: Encode the latents first, in the Latent cache card above — every stage here reads the manifest that writes.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.allowNoMintedHint: The run is refused without this, and the held-out minted loss — the one number that separates learning the style from memorising the songs — is not produced at all.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.mintedEntry: The entry is "YuE2 Minted Regulariser Pack" on the YuE2 tab.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.mintedMissing: The minted regulariser pack is not installed. Half of every batch is meant to be true YuE2 tokens, and that mix is the counterweight to a real defect: our semantic encoder repeats adjacent codes far more often than YuE2's own, which is out of distribution in the direction that produces LOOPING.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.trainBlurb: Trains a LoRA on the AR half from whole songs — no crops, so nothing teaches the model that a song may begin mid-flow. Snapshots are plain safetensors files you can load straight into the YuE2 adapter field. The engine is paused for the run.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.runsHalted: This run still holds its optimizer state, which means it stopped before its clean finish — the engine deletes that file on export. Continuing a run is not wired up here; start a fresh one with the same recipe.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.runsBlurb: Every composer LoRA this dataset has produced. Each rung is a plain safetensors file — copy a path into the YuE2 adapter field to hear it. Step {{pick}} is where the ear landed on the reference run, which is a starting point and not a verdict on yours.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.alignCpuHint: Several times slower, and both backends pass the port's gates. It cannot be changed once the run starts.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.alignCpu: Run the aligner on the CPU
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.alignOnlyHint: Also the re-run mechanism: this stage has no force flag, so name the source whose lyrics you edited.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.stemsDirHint: Blank uses the dataset's own. A path you type has to exist — the engine's answer to a wrong one is to skip every source and exit cleanly.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.alignBlurb: Force-aligns each song's lyrics against its vocal stem and caches where every word is sung. That is what the cursor loss is measured against, and it is measured to matter — with it the frame-to-lyric alignment loss fell where without it it rose. Optional only if you turn the cursor weight down to 0.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.alignNeedsLatents: Encode the latents first — the lyrics the spans are measured against come out of that manifest.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.alignNoStems: Separation happens outside this stage, so the stems are an input it cannot produce. It wants <source stem>/vocals.wav per song and skips by name, so with none of them it would align nothing and still report success — the run is refused instead. Run the Vocal stems stage just above, or point Advanced's stems folder at stems you already have.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.alignNoLyrics: The latent cache was built with clip captions set to "{{mode}}", so it carries no lyrics and this stage has nothing to align: it would skip every source and fail. Re-encode the latents with clip captions set to the YuE2 mode (or "ace") — the sidecars beside the audio already hold the lyrics, and the AR half needs the captions anyway, since the caption is its prefix.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.alignMissing: Missing: {{files}}. The aligner has no Model Manager entry yet, so it has to be placed in {{dir}} by hand.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.stemsForceHint: Off, a song whose stem is already on disk is skipped, which is what makes a resumed run cheap. Turn it on only after changing the source audio or the level.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.stemsLevelHint: Which SuperSep pass separates the vocal. The aligner opens one file, vocals.wav, so the default runs the separator with everything but the vocal stem masked off, in one pass. The six-stem split produces a drum kit and a piano this stage then deletes, at roughly three model passes instead of one — slower for no benefit to this stage.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.stemsLive: Separating now — the count below is live.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.stemsBlurb: Separates each song's vocal and writes it as <source>/vocals.wav, which is the only thing the aligner below reads. It is a separate stage because separation costs minutes a track while alignment costs seconds, and because it is worth doing once: a stem already on disk is skipped.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.stemsNeedsLatents: Encode the latents first — this stage separates the sources that manifest names.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sheetSoftFail: This source soft-failed to render a lead sheet: {{error}}
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sheetTrackNone: No lead sheet for this source.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sheetTrackInfo: Chooses which source's lead sheet and original audio show below. It only picks what this preview shows — it starts no job and changes nothing that gets trained.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sheetFastHint: Skips the exact-load precision fix. Leave off unless you have measured that the default matters for your corpus.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sheetForceHint: Off, lead sheets already beside the audio (the .abc files the Label step saves) or already in the cache are reused and only the missing ones are transcribed. On, every source is transcribed again and its .abc is replaced.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sheetHave: {{done}} of {{total}} source(s) have a lead sheet, {{failed}} soft-failed (abc_error).
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sheetBlurb: Transcribes each source's own audio into a SheetSage2 lead sheet (chords + melody), which --abc-dropout on both trainers reads to draw the cot=full conditioning instead of cot=off. Optional: a source with no lead sheet simply always trains cot=off, same as before this stage existed. Roughly 4% of real tracks decode fine but fail to render — that shows up as "soft-failed", not an error, and those sources also always train cot=off.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sheetLiveNote: Lead sheets appear here as each source finishes.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.sheetMissing: Missing: {{files}}. Install it from the Model Manager (yue2-sheetsage2-f16) — nothing in generation needs it, so a fresh install will not have it.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.tokForceHint: Off, an already complete source is skipped — which is what makes a resumed run cheap.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.decodeHint: Which decoder reads the source audio before tokenizing it. Must match what the latent cache used: the codes and the latents are only frame-aligned because both came from identically decoded samples.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.tokMixed: These codes came from {{had}} and the installed tokenizer is now {{have}}. Two tokenizers across one cache is one corpus with two vocabularies — re-run with "Re-encode cached sources" ticked.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.tokHave: {{done}} of {{total}} source(s) have codes, {{clips}} of {{clipTotal}} clip(s).
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.tokBlurb: Runs the sources the latent cache already names back through the semantic tokenizer and caches the codec ids. These are the TARGETS the AR half learns to predict, so without them there is nothing for it to train on. Re-running is cheap: a source whose codes are already complete is skipped.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.needsLatents: Encode the latents first — this stage reads the manifest preprocess writes, not the source folder.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2ar.tokMissing: Missing: {{files}}. Install it from the Model Manager (yue2-tok-f16) — nothing in generation needs it, so a fresh install will not have it.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.ladderHint: Every saved checkpoint is a rung. Previews render while the run trains: by default one 300 s draft take of the dataset's first sung track per rung, on the same seed every rung, so the rungs sing roughly the same song and what changes between them is the training; compare rungs on it. Takes per checkpoint adds more, each on a new random seed: a song no other rung made, which shows how the checkpoint does on a fresh draw and catches failures the fixed seed happens to miss. A rung with no previews yet says so, and Render adds takes. Score likeness and corruption 1-5, then press Use this rung on your pick: it becomes the dataset's adapter and you can clean up the rest. Scores also feed the Review page and "Finish scored" for batches.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.ladderRunInfo: This dataset has more than one joint run. Pick which run's ladder to listen to and score. Each run keeps its own scores.
translation.trainingStudio.review.originInfo: Trained on this worker and mirrored here; previews and scoring run here.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.awaitingMirro: Waiting for the first sync from {{worker}}
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.plannerFrozen: Planner frozen at step {{step}} (KL target reached). The decoder is still training, faster: the loss and KL lines end here, the step counter and pace below keep moving.
translation.trainingStudio.workers.runOnInfo: A training worker trains the batch on its own GPU. Each dataset is captioned here first (Gemini, when captioning is on), its audio and sidecars are sent to the worker (only files it does not already have), and it joins the worker's batch. Switch "Train on" at the top to that worker to follow the run. The ladder, its previews and scoring stay here: they open on this run once it lands in this machine's own index.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.aitkBatch.clearCache: Deletes each dataset's YuE2 caches (latents, codes, lead sheets, vocal stems, lyric timing, prepared datasets) before it starts, so everything is rebuilt from the audio. Source audio, captions and trained adapters are not touched. Each album then takes as long as a first-time preparation.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.aitkBatch.draftHint: Each dataset runs its caches, lead sheets, timing (when enabled), preparation and joint training in order with this recipe. The batch runs on the server; the page follows the dataset being trained.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.aitkBatch.draftTitle: Batch: these settings apply to {{count}} dataset(s)
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewCaptio: Replaces the preview track's own caption for the rendered sample. Leave blank to use the track's caption as-is.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewContro: Also renders a fixed reference take at every checkpoint, for a stable point of comparison as the adapter trains.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewBaseli: Also renders a take from the unmodified base model alongside the adapter, so you can hear what the adapter changed.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewSongHi: The caption comes from the first sung track in this dataset. Caption and lyrics overrides below replace either choice.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewLyrics: Lyric Studio generation (falls back to dataset lyrics)
Replaces the preview track's own lyrics for the rendered sample. Leave blank to use the track's lyrics as-is.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewArScal: Music adapter strength for checkpoint previews, including manual renders. Default 0.6. The sound (NAR) adapter stays at 1.0.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewTakesI: How many preview tracks each checkpoint renders, 1 to 4. Take 1 uses the preview seed, so it compares like for like across checkpoints; every extra take uses a fresh random seed. Each take adds its render time to every checkpoint.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewSeedIn: The random seed used for every preview render, so previews across checkpoints are directly comparable rather than each landing on a different random take.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewSecond: How long the rendered preview sample is, from 8 to 120 seconds. Longer previews show more of the song but take longer to render at every checkpoint.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewEngine: The engine is stopped during training, so only the final checkpoint gets a preview automatically; render the other rungs from the ladder after the run.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.previewParall: Render each checkpoint's preview while training continues; needs the engine up (this also turns "Stop the engine during training" off). Off: training pauses at each checkpoint, renders, and resumes, which fits a smaller card but takes longer.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.stopEngineHel: Off by default since the ladder previews render while training runs and need the engine up (about 14 GB for the trainer plus 10-12 GB for the engine and a render). On: the trainer gets the whole GPU, generation is unavailable, and no previews render until the run ends; use it on a smaller card and render the ladder afterwards.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.reconTargetIn: Also stop once the reconstruction meter is at or under this. Blank: the plateau alone decides.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.reconKeepDelt: A decoder-phase checkpoint is kept only if its reconstruction beats the best so far by at least this much. 0 keeps every checkpoint.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.reconStopWind: How many checkpoints the gain line is fitted over. Wider smooths noise but reacts later.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.reconStopInfo: Stop once the reconstruction meter improves by less than this fraction over the window. 0 trains to the budget.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.narExtraSteps: The most steps the decoder trains alone after the freeze. The plateau stop usually ends it sooner; Updates caps it too.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.decoderPhaseI: At the KL target the planner freezes instead of the run ending, and the decoder (timbre, where likeness lives) trains alone until its reconstruction meter flattens: the gain over the last few checkpoints, read off a fitted line, drops under the minimum below. It is the plateau test the Refine page used. A decoder checkpoint whose reconstruction did not beat the best so far by the keep threshold is deleted, so the ladder keeps only real gains. Updates is still the cap. Needs "Train until" on the AR KL target.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.decoderPhase: Train the decoder on after the KL stop
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lrCycleMultIn: How much longer each sgdr cycle is than the last. 1 keeps them equal.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lrCycleStepsI: The length of the first sgdr cycle, in steps.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lrDecayShapeI: The curve of the wsd decay: linear steps down evenly; cosine eases in and out.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.klOvershootMa: How far the KL may pass the target during the decay before the stop acts at once instead of waiting for the decay to finish.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lrDecayStepsI: How many steps the wsd decay lasts once a stop triggers it. Longer is a gentler anneal.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lrFloorInfo: Where the cosine decay ends, as a fraction of the learning rate, instead of zero.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lrScheduleInf: How the learning rate changes over the run. cosine and linear decay to zero at the step cap, so a run that stops early on its KL keeps the weights mid-decay. wsd stays flat until a stop is near, then decays for a set number of steps so the kept weights are annealed. constant stays flat. sgdr cycles the rate in growing loops.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.spikeStopWind: How many steps the skipped updates must fall within to end the run.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.spikeStopInfo: End the run when this many updates are skipped within the window, keeping the last pre-spike weights. 0 never stops on spikes alone.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.spikeFactorIn: Skip any update whose gradient norm is over this many times the recent median, so one bad step cannot corrupt the adapter. 0 turns the guard off.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.captionDropou: The share of steps trained on the trigger word alone instead of the song's full caption, so a new caption at generation time still lands on the artist. 0 trains on the caption every step.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.klWeightInfo: How strongly the planner loss is pulled back toward the base model each step. Higher keeps the planner closer to the base (safer, less likeness); lower lets it drift further per step.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.narLrScaleInf: The decoder (NAR, where timbre and likeness live) half trains at the learning rate × this. Lower it if renders garble words or lose audio quality.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.plannerLrScal: The planner (AR) half trains at the learning rate × this. Higher reaches the KL target sooner; lower is gentler and less prone to planner damage.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.targetLossInf: Stops the run once the trailing 20-step mean of the composite loss (AR CE + KL weight × AR KL + NAR flow MSE) is at or below this. Lower trains longer.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.targetKlModeI: How the KL target is read off the training curve. The 30-step trend line reacts at once to where the curve is heading; the 20-step mean is smoother but lags about 10 steps, so the run trains a little past the target before it notices.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.targetKlField: How far the planner may move from the base model before the run stops (or the planner freezes, with the decoder phase below on). Higher trains a stronger likeness but risks planner damage (looping outros); lower stays safer but weaker.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.stopModeInfo: What ends the run: an AR KL target (the planner has moved a set distance from the base model), a plain step count, or a target loss. Legacy uses the KL target, the tested stop. Updates is the cap either way.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.legacyLockedH: Only the Legacy preset uses these; base-matched fixes its own values.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.arCropInfo: The planner trains on only the first this-many frames of each song (25 per second) instead of the whole song. The planner backward is the largest cost of an update, so this is the biggest speed lever, but the planner then never trains on the rest of the song or its ending, and whole songs are what fixed endings and structure in this recipe. It only applies while the decoder crop is on (not 0), and a song shorter than the decoder crop still trains whole. Untested by ear. 0 or blank trains whole songs.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.bmNarCropInfo: The decoder trains on this many frames per song (25 per second). 0 trains on the whole song, as the base did (about 12 GB of VRAM and 11-15 s a step on a 4-minute song). Every preset uses 1500, a 60 s crop: about 40% faster, and it scored as well as whole songs in a blind test.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.bmAbcDropoutI: Share of steps trained without the lead sheet, matching the report's balanced mix of tasks with and without a score.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.bothDropoutIn: Share of steps trained on the bare instruction with no style or lyrics: exactly the prompt the runtime's guidance uses as its unconditional branch.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lyricDropoutI: Share of steps trained with the lyrics removed and the style kept, written the way the official instrumental tooling sends a lyric-free request.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.textDropoutIn: Share of steps trained with the style text (trigger included) removed and the lyrics kept. The report drops text and lyrics separately or together for guidance but gives no rates; 0.1 is the agreed default.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.beta2Info: How long the optimizer's second moment remembers. The report's joint phase used 0.95; torch's 0.999 is what the tuned recipe uses.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.arLossWeightI: The planner's cross-entropy is weighted by this against the decoder's flow loss before the shared gradient clip, so it sets how much of the clip the planner takes. The report trains the base at 0.25; 1.0 is the tuned recipe.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.gradAccumInfo: Gradients of this many songs are averaged before each optimizer update, so one step sees more than one song, as the base's batch of 256 did. Each update takes this many times longer. Fast and Balanced use 4 (about 17 s an update on the 5090 with 60 s decoder crops, 28 s with whole songs), Thorough 8 (about twice that). 1 updates on every song.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.bmWeightDecay: Decoupled weight decay, as the base's joint phase used.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.warmupInfo: Linear warmup to the peak rate, then cosine decay to a 0.1x floor at the step count. Blank = 3% of the steps, the base's own joint-phase warmup share.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.bmLrInfo: AdamW peak learning rate for both halves. The report gives full-model rates only (3e-4 joint, annealed to 3e-5), which do not transfer to an adapter; 1e-4 is the agreed default.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.baseMatchedKn: Blank uses the default shown in grey. The report does not state a fine-tuning learning rate or the dropout rates, so those defaults are agreed guesses; the rest are the report's own values.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.legacyKnobsHi: Legacy runs the previous recipe: a blank field below uses that recipe's own value, not the grey one.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.sizeEstimate: Expected adapter size: {{total}} for both halves ({{half}} each for the planner and the decoder).
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.sizeBadFactor: This LoKr factor does not split the attention and MLP outputs on their boundaries, so training will refuse it. Try 4 or 8.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.alphaInfo: The LoRA scale. This card keeps it equal to rank (scale 1); raising alpha above rank strengthens the adapter's effect without changing its size.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.rankInfo: The size of the low-rank adapter pair. Higher gives more capacity to learn the artist, at a larger file and more VRAM; lower trains a smaller, less expressive adapter.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lokrAlphaInfo: The LoKr strength, alpha / dim. The presets use 256 at dim 128 (a scale of 2); the earlier dim-64 recipe used 256 at dim 64. Raise dim for more capacity rather than raising alpha alone.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lokrFactorInf: How each weight is split into two Kronecker factors: the smaller factor is at most this size. 4 is tested; 8 also fits. At factor 4, stay below dim 256, where some sites stop factorizing and ignore alpha.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.lokrDimInfo: The size of the Kronecker-factored delta. Higher gives the adapter more capacity, at a larger file and more VRAM. The presets use 128 with alpha 256 (about 213 MB for both halves; 64 is about 106 MB).
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.seedInfo: The random seed for training (batch order, dropout, initial noise). Changing it gives a different run on the same data; keeping it fixed makes a rerun reproducible.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.saveEveryInfo: How many steps between saved checkpoints. Lower gives more rungs to pick from (and more previews, if enabled) at the cost of disk space and time; higher saves less often. The presets save ten rungs: every 10 on Fast, 20 on Balanced, 30 on Thorough.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.saveEveryKlIn: Steps saves a checkpoint every N steps. AR KL saves a rung each time the planner KL crosses the next multiple of the value, up to the KL target, with previews on each. Once the planner freezes at the target the KL stops moving, so the decoder phase saves (and previews) every {{steps}} steps.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.stepsInfo: How many optimizer updates to train. Each update averages "songs per update" songs, so Fast (100 × 4) sees 400 songs, Balanced (200 × 4) 800 and Thorough (300 × 8) 2400. The run ends here; pick a checkpoint by ear.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.adapterTypeIn: The adapter parameterization trained. LoRA is the standard low-rank pair. LoKr trains a Kronecker-factored delta per site instead, at a similar file size for more capacity; it is the default and what every preset was tested with. DoRA is a LoRA pair plus a learned magnitude per output row, so it uses the LoRA rank and alpha; it is untested on this model and needs a little more VRAM and time per update. Switching resets rank/alpha (or dim/factor/alpha) and the KL stop to that type's tested defaults.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.deviceInfo: The ggml device for this run, such as Vulkan0 or Vulkan1. Leave empty for the first GPU.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.baseInfo: The frozen model the adapters train against. ConvRot (int8) is the checkpoint the recipe was tuned and ear-tested on, and needs a CUDA build. A GGUF base runs on any GPU: bf16 is full precision, and the quantized files trade a little accuracy for a lot of memory (Q4_K_M holds the base in about 2 GB). The adapter works with every base at generation time.

translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.presetImportT: Add presets from a .json file exported here or by someone else
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.presetExport: Download this preset as a .json file to share or back up
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.presetUpdate: Overwrite this preset with the current settings
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.presetLegacyN: Legacy runs the previous recipe (Prodigy, one song per update, stops at planner KL 1.0, LoKr 256). It may train faster, but quality will not be as good as the new presets: they fixed the endings, structure and late-run degradation this recipe has. Lyric timing is off and the audio cache is not re-cut for it, so it is close to the old recipe rather than exact.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.fixedRecipeNo: The server fixes the adapter, optimizer, loss, crop and timing settings for this method. The base defaults to bf16 and can be changed below.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.fixedRecipeBa: Not ear-tested on this base: HOT-Approved was tuned and scored on bf16. A quantized base uses less VRAM.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.presetInfo: Fast, Balanced and Thorough are the same recipe; they differ in how many updates run, how many songs each update averages, and how often a checkpoint is saved (each saves ten). All three train the decoder on 60 s crops. Legacy is the previous recipe: one song per update, stopping once the planner has moved a set distance from the base model, so it can finish sooner, but its adapters scored lower by ear than the three new presets. Each preset shows its time relative to Balanced. For scale, Balanced takes about an hour on a 15-track album on an RTX 5090; a slower GPU or a longer album takes proportionally longer.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.resumeDataset: The prepared dataset manifest that matches the run being resumed by record below. Filled in automatically when a resume record is set; only needed if you are pointing at a different prepared copy.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.sheetsageInfo: On-disk path to the SheetSage lead-sheet model used during preparation. Usually filled in automatically once installed in Model Manager.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.semanticInfo: On-disk path to the semantic tokenizer model used during preparation. Usually filled in automatically once installed in Model Manager.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.vaeInfo: On-disk path to the YuE2 VAE checkpoint used to encode audio during preparation. Usually filled in automatically once installed in Model Manager.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.prepareOutput: Where native preparation writes the converted dataset (latents, codes, lead sheets). Leave the default unless you want a second prepared copy of this dataset.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.tokenizerInfo: On-disk path to the YuE2 text/audio tokenizer used to prepare the dataset. Usually filled in automatically once the YuE2 training assets are installed.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.legacyManifes: On-disk path to the legacy YuE2 manifest that native preparation converts from. Usually filled in automatically from the dataset; set it by hand only to prepare from a different manifest.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.captioning: Captioning tracks without a YuE2 caption: {{done}} / {{total}}
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.calibratedInf: Experimental. Sizes the run to the album instead of using the preset as it is: the preset's updates and save interval are scaled by the album's minutes of audio against a 45-minute album (between 0.6× and 2×), so the ladder keeps the same number of rungs. A 53-minute album on a 200-update preset trains for 240 updates. The rule came from ear-scored ladders of the earlier recipe, where longer albums took longer to reach full likeness; runs with this on test whether it holds for this one. The training log says what it chose, and the run records it. Off: the preset runs exactly as shown. Applies to new runs, single and batch.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.autoCaptionNo: No captioner available: add a Gemini key in Settings → AI Services or install MOSS. Tracks without a .yue2.txt train on the long ACE caption.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.autoCaptionHi: Before training, tracks without a .yue2.txt are re-captioned from the audio (ACE, MM3 and YuE2 captions; lyrics and BPM are left alone). Skipped when every track has one. Off: trains on the long ACE caption for those tracks instead.
translation.trainingStudio.yue2.method.autoCaption: Caption tracks that have no YuE2 caption

Pick "Start a new run" to train from scratch instead; a run with no saved optimizer state, or one still running, cannot be resumed.

translation.cover.prepare.structure.hearRecordingInf: Plays the source recording from one bar before the selection to its end. The position is worked out from the score's own tempo, so it can drift from the real recording.

translation.cover.prepare.structure.nameInfo: The section's label in the score. Renaming never changes the music or the lyric words.
translation.cover.prepare.structure.mergedNameInfo: The label of the merged section. It starts as the first section's label.
translation.cover.prepare.structure.atBarInfo: The bar where a split, or the moved boundary, starts a section. Pick it from the bar numbers below or type it.
translation.cover.prepare.structure.newNameInfo: The label of the second half after a split.

translation.cover.prepare.structure.toBarInfo: The last bar of the run to rewrite.

Essentia is the older CPU estimate, which often halves or doubles the tempo. If beat_this is not installed, Essentia is used.
translation.trainingStudio.label.keySourceInfo: SheetSage2 (default) transcribes a lead sheet for each track that has none and reads the key from it: 22 of 23 right on the check, against 11 for Essentia. The lead sheet is saved beside the audio as an .abc file, with its tempo replaced by beat_this's when beat_this is the tempo source, ready for YuE2 covers. It is a GPU pass of a few seconds per track that runs alongside beat_this, Genius and MOSS, so each track moves on as soon as its own lead sheet is done. If the transcriber is not installed, Essentia's key is used.
translation.trainingStudio.label.tempoBoundsError: Use 40–180 for minimum, 60–250 for maximum, with minimum below maximum.

translation.trainingStudio.label.mergePolicyInfo: How a new result is combined with data a track already has. Keep what's there only fills in blanks and never touches an existing value; the other options overwrite captions, lyrics, or everything with this run's results.
translation.trainingStudio.label.useGeniusInfo: Fetches each track's real lyrics from Genius by title and artist. Off: this pass is skipped and lyrics are left at whatever the dataset already has.
translation.trainingStudio.label.localLyricsInfo: Each track with no lyrics (after Genius, if that is on) is transcribed from its audio by Music Flamingo, with [Verse]/[Chorus] section tags. Tracks marked instrumental are left alone, and so are lyrics already in a sidecar unless the merge policy overwrites lyrics, which re-transcribes them (the way to move a dataset off Genius). A transcript that loops is redone once with a light repetition penalty. Runs on your GPU, about 5 seconds a track on a fast card.
translation.trainingStudio.enhance.normaliseLyricsHi: Rewrites every section tag to [Intro] [Verse] [Pre-Chorus] [Chorus] [Post-Chorus] [Bridge] [Breakdown] [Interlude] [Instrumental] [Outro], unnumbered. Speaker tags and stage directions go; the words stay. Each changed sidecar is backed up first.
translation.trainingStudio.enhance.retag: Recover missing sections from the audio (Music Flamingo)
translation.trainingStudio.enhance.retagInfo: For lyrics with no section tags at all: Music Flamingo transcribes the track with tags, the transcript is lined up with your lyrics word by word, and the section starts are copied across. Your words are kept. About 5 seconds a track on the GPU.
translation.trainingStudio.enhance.normaliseBlocked: Recovering sections from audio needs the card, which the running training job owns. Turn it off or wait.
translation.trainingStudio.label.useCaptionInfo: Sends each track as a small MP3 so an AI describes what it actually hears and writes a caption and genre. Only Gemini and the local MOSS captioner listen to the audio; other cloud providers work from title, artist and lyrics only. Off: this pass is skipped and caption/genre are left at whatever the dataset already has.

With a locked dataset sample selected, the audition sends the trainer's own lyrics instead and this box is read-only. translation.trainingStudio.audition.sidesInfo: The runs compared in this audition: a left side and, when Compare two sides is on, a right side next to it. Each side can point at the base LM or at a planner adapter, so you can judge an adapter against the base, or two adapters against each other.
translation.trainingStudio.audition.twoSidedInfo: On: runs both sides and shows a right-hand slot next to the base LM, so you hear them side by side. Off: runs only the left side, for auditioning one LM or adapter alone.

translation.trainingStudio.audition.seedInfo: The LM seed for both sides of this audition. Blank draws a random seed each run; the dice button rolls a fixed one. Using the same seed on both sides isolates the adapter as the only difference between them.
translation.trainingStudio.audition.durationInfo: How many seconds of audio codes the LM plans for this audition. Longer takes longer to plan and decode but lets you judge structure over more of the song; the server clamps it to 10-300 either way.
translation.trainingStudio.audition.temperatureInfo: How much randomness the LM uses when picking each audio code. Higher is more varied and less predictable; lower sticks closer to the LM's most likely choice each step.
translation.trainingStudio.audition.topPInfo: Nucleus sampling threshold: only the smallest set of most-likely codes whose probabilities add up to this value are eligible at each step. Lower narrows the LM to safer, more predictable choices; higher allows more variety.
translation.trainingStudio.audition.cfgScaleInfo: Guidance strength for the LM itself, how closely it follows the caption and lyrics versus drifting on its own. Higher pushes it closer to the prompt; lower lets it wander more freely.
translation.trainingStudio.audition.repPenaltyInfo: Penalises audio codes the LM used recently, over roughly a 13-second window, so it does not get stuck in a loop. 1.0 turns it off; higher pushes harder against repetition, which can also flatten deliberate structure like a chorus coming back.
translation.trainingStudio.audition.adapterScaleInfo: How strongly the right-hand side's planner adapter is applied. 1.0 is full strength as trained; lower fades toward the base LM's behaviour, higher exaggerates the adapter past what it was trained at.
translation.trainingStudio.audition.baseScaleInfo: Scales the left side's adapter strength the same way Adapter scale does for the right side. Only has an effect when the Base LM field above also has an adapter selected.
translation.trainingStudio.audition.coResidentHint: Keeps the LM resident between the two runs. That flips the engine to never-evict for the rest of its lifetime — the same thing the Create panel's co-resident toggle does. The LM is unloaded again when the job ends.
