translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.deleteConfirm: Delete the tensor cache for {{variant}}? The audio and dataset.json are untouched.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.baseModelInfo: The DiT checkpoint the encoded tensors are tied to. Training against this base produces an adapter that only loads correctly on the same base at generation time.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.vaeInfo: The VAE used to encode each song's audio into latents during preprocessing. Must match the VAE you generate with, or the adapter's latents will not line up with what the DiT expects.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.textEncoderInf: The text encoder that turns each song's caption and lyrics into the hidden states preprocessing bakes into the cache. Changing it after caching means re-running preprocessing.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.maxDurationMet: default 600s, matches the engine's 10-minute generation ceiling
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.maxDurationInf: Songs are hard-cut to this length before encoding; anything longer loses everything past the cut. Raising it lets longer songs train whole, at the cost of more VRAM and time per song. Lowering it below a song's real length teaches the adapter a false ending at the cut point.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.normalizeInfo: Whether each song's audio is peak-normalized to the target level before encoding. Peak evens out loudness differences across your dataset; none encodes the audio as-is, which is closer to Side-Step's original behaviour but lets quiet or loud source tracks skew what the adapter learns.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.targetDbInfo: The peak level, in dBFS, that Normalize scales each song's audio to. Raising it (toward 0) makes the cached audio louder before encoding; lowering it leaves more headroom. It has no effect when Normalize is off.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.dtypeInfo: The numeric precision the encoded tensor cache is stored in. f32 is the exact reference cache; bf16 halves the cache's disk size at a small precision loss. Switching it means re-encoding, since the two caches are not interchangeable.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.compatInfo: How the caption and lyric prompt text is assembled for the text encoder. HOT-Step matches what this app conditions on at generation time. Side-Step parity reproduces the older Side-Step trainer's prompt format instead — for debugging cross-trainer differences, not for adapters meant to run in this app.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.maxCaptionToke: The longest caption, in tokens, the text encoder will keep; anything past this is truncated before encoding. Raising it preserves longer captions in full; lowering it risks silently cutting real caption content, which was the bug that pushed the default up from Side-Step's 256.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.maxLyricTokens: The longest lyric sheet, in tokens, kept before truncation. Raising it preserves full lyrics on longer songs; lowering it truncates lyrics on the songs that need the most tokens first.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.vaeChunkInfo: How many latent frames the VAE encodes per tile when it processes a song's audio. Larger tiles use more VRAM per step; smaller tiles use less VRAM but do more tiling work. It changes memory use only, not the audio the cache holds.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.vaeOverlapInfo: How many latent frames of overlap the VAE keeps on each side of a tile boundary, to hide the seam between tiles. Raising it smooths tile boundaries at some extra VRAM and compute cost; lowering it risks an audible seam on long songs.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.overwriteInfo: Re-encodes songs that already have a cached tensor set, instead of skipping them. Off (default), a repeated preprocess run only encodes songs that are missing or changed, which is faster; on, it redoes every song, which is what you want after changing a setting on this form.
translation.trainingStudio.preprocess.stopEngineInfo: Shuts the engine down for the duration of the preprocessing job so the VAE and text encoder can use its VRAM, then restarts it automatically when the job ends. Off, preprocessing runs alongside the engine, which can run out of VRAM depending on your GPU and models. Generation is unavailable while the engine is stopped.

translation.trainingStudio.train.lmSizeHint4B: 4B trains in low-VRAM mode (gradient checkpointing + chunked loss) — around 12 GB, and slower per step than 1.7B.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lmVramHintLow: Low-VRAM mode: ~{{est}} MB estimated peak of {{free}} MB free, max sequence {{maxLen}} tokens ({{base}} MB base + {{ckpt}} MB checkpoints + {{seg}} MB per segment).
translation.trainingStudio.train.lmVramHintNaive: Standard mode: ~{{est}} MB estimated peak of {{free}} MB free, max sequence {{maxLen}} tokens.
translation.trainingStudio.train.adapterNameInvalid: Use only letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores (max 64), not starting with a dot.

translation.trainingStudio.train.targetLossHelp: Training stops as soon as an epoch's average loss reaches this. Max epochs is only a backstop.
translation.trainingStudio.train.maxEpochsHelp: Hard cap. Reached only if the target loss never is.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.scheduleSummary: {{steps}} optimizer steps total (effective batch {{effectiveBatch}}, warmup ~{{warmup}} steps)
translation.trainingStudio.train.weightsHint: Experimental, and it has NOT passed its own acceptance gates. bf16 runs the frozen projections in BF16 instead of casting them to F32: measured 1.26x per micro-step at 4B, 1.03x at 0.6B, and about 100 MB less VRAM. But its gradient-parity checks come in over their limits — worst element 12% off the F32 gradient against a 2% limit, direction 0.9995 against a 0.9999 limit — so a bf16 adapter is a genuinely different train, not a faster identical one. It also needs a BF16 base and low-VRAM mode. Leave on f32-window unless you are A/B testing by ear.
translation.trainingStudio.train.bwdHint: How the activation gradient is computed. outprod is upstream ggml's out_prod, which on CUDA only runs in F32 — so the frozen weight has to be F32 and the forward pass gets dragged onto slower TF32 maths with it. mm computes exactly the same gradient a different way, and it works on any dtype, so a BF16 weight can use the card's BF16 tensor cores in both directions. Measured 1.7-1.8x faster per layer per step on an RTX 5090, with the gradient matching the F32 reference to within about 0.4%. This is not a quality trade like the projection-weights setting above: both options compute the same quantity. Only switch to outprod if you suspect the fast path.
translation.trainingStudio.train.bwdHintLm: How the activation gradient is computed. Leave this on outprod unless you also set projection weights to f32-window. The bf16 projection-weights setting above already gives this trainer the fast mul_mat backward, by a different internal route, and the two cannot be combined — picking both is refused rather than silently ignored.
translation.trainingStudio.train.batchHint: Fixed at 1 — micro-batching is not built. It was measured before being written: batching cannot make the maths cheaper, it only spreads per-step host overhead across samples, and at 4B that overhead is 9% of a step — less than the 10% the design required to justify the work, and it would be partly eaten by padding waste. Use gradient accumulation to change the effective batch size instead.

translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.attnBackendInfo: Routes attention through the same fused ggml_flash_attn_train/_back kernels the DiT trainer uses, instead of today's manual softmax chain. New for the LM (2026-09-02) and not validated by ear yet. On by default, as on the DiT. The key/value prefix needs exact attention, so with Train an artist token on and Prefix columns above 0 (the default) the run trains exact anyway. Exact stays bit-identical to every older run; flash is expected to drift slightly, the same way `--bwd mm` does.

translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.title: Sound LoRA (DiT)
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.statusUnavailab: Could not read this dataset's DiT training status — reopen the dataset to retry.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.minVram: Needs a 16 GB GPU (24 GB for full depth). Smaller cards are refused before training starts.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.channelStatsMis: No channel_stats.json in this variant — the Channel balance switch will have no effect.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.subtitle: Teaches the audio model itself your dataset's sound — tone, production and instrumentation.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.baseModelHelp: Fixed by the preprocessed tensors — they are this model's own output, so training against another base would be meaningless.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.targetLossHelp: Training stops as soon as the 5-epoch average loss reaches this. Max epochs is only a backstop.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.adapterTypeHelp: LoKR (Kronecker-factored) is the recommended default — it trains faster and smaller at equivalent quality. DoRA, HiRA, LoHa and HRA are LoRA with a different parameterization and save as LoRA-family adapters; hover a button for what each one measured. PiSSA (init), rsLoRA (scaling) and LoRA+ (learning-rate ratio) modify whichever LoRA-family method is picked. Switching between LoKR and the LoRA family resets the fields below to that family's defaults.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.lokrFactorHelp: -1 lets the factorization pick the most balanced split automatically.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.targetMlpHelp: Adds gate/up/down to the eight attention sites. On by default — most of a record's timbre lives there. It costs VRAM, so the auto-fit will shorten the audio window to pay for it.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.attnBackendInfo: Routes attention through fused kernels so training crops can reach full-song length instead of the ~50 s cap — the auto-fit picks the crop, and the max-crop cap lifts to the dataset's longest track. On by default; ticking it unpins the crop cap, and unticking restores the exact graph with the classic 1250-frame cap. Costs some per-step speed.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.attnBackendHelp: Full-song training crops via fused attention. Untick for the pre-2026-09 exact graph (bit-identical to older runs).
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.cropJitterInfo: Each training draw picks a crop length between Window minimum and the fitted crop, instead of always taking the longest window that fits. Off, every step trains on a long crop and a quiet intro or breakdown gets buried inside it rather than a whole optimizer step of its own; long crops without this measurably under-render quiet passages (2026-09-03). On, shorter crops appear more often, giving quiet sections their own steps. Experimental, off by default.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.paramGroupHelp: Plain LoRA is the default because nothing beat it in the 2026-09-04 blind test on one album dataset (five arms, three full songs): LoRA, HiRA and PiSSA tied within listening noise, rsLoRA is the same method, DoRA came last. Costs per epoch at rank 128: LoRA-class ~1x, DoRA ~1.1x, HiRA ~1.5x, LoHa ~3x, HRA ~4x at 8 reflections. HiRA, LoHa and HRA merge into the model rather than running as a low-rank overlay.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.doraInfo: Weight-decomposed LoRA: a learned per-output magnitude on top of the LoRA direction. In practice it pins each row's norm while the direction moves. Blind test: last of five on all three songs, though it led a sighted 60-second comparison — judge it blind. Exports lora_magnitude_vector.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.hiraInfo: Hadamard high-rank adaptation: the base weight modulates the LoRA update (W + W ⊙ BA), so the effective rank is not capped by r. Lowest training loss of the set and never below 2nd in the blind test, at ~1.5x the time per epoch. Merge mode only.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.lohaInfo: LyCORIS LoHa: two LoRA pairs multiplied element-wise, effective rank up to r². Same loss trajectory as LoRA at ~3x the time and twice the file. Exported in the LyCORIS hada_w* layout. Merge mode only.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.rsloraInfo: Rank-stabilised scaling alpha/√r instead of alpha/r. At a matched strength it is the same model as LoRA (identical loss trajectory, blind-test scores within noise); its purpose is keeping the learning dynamics constant when you sweep rank. Written to the adapter config so it merges at the trained strength.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.loraPlusRatioIn: B tensors learn at this multiple of A's learning rate (the paper's 16). Fixes the A-random / B-zero asymmetry. Measured on this DiT: the same loss trajectory as plain LoRA to within 3 epochs. 1 = off. AdamW-rule optimizers only; Muon ignores it.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.pissaInfo: Starts A and B on the weight's own top-r singular directions and keeps the residual in the base, so training fine-tunes the principal subspace from step one. Exports as a normal LoRA of rank 2r (BF16; an F32 export was indistinguishable by ear and twice the size). Blind test on one album dataset: tied with plain LoRA at double the file. Plain LoRA only; a PiSSA run cannot be resumed.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.hraInfo: Householder Reflection Adaptation: each site's input is rotated by a product of `rank` learned reflections before the frozen weight, so the update is orthogonal and the weight's spectrum is preserved. Rank must be even. Very small adapter (38 MB at 8 reflections) but ~4x the time per epoch and a much weaker change than a LoRA. Exports as an exact rank-r LoRA.
translation.trainingStudio.train.softPromptGroupHelp: A named token adds k learned vectors behind a placeholder in every caption; the prefix adds n key/value columns per layer. Both train with the LoRA, ship in the same adapter file and apply automatically at generation. They learn ~50× faster than the LoRA, so the target loss fires early — set it to 0 for a joint run. In a probe on one album dataset, k=32 beat k=8 on every code-distribution metric; neither is ear-validated yet.
translation.trainingStudio.train.artistTokenOnInfo: On by default: the adapter ships with a learned token and a key/value prefix trained alongside the LoRA. Arm 05 of the 2026-09-04 listening test (this recipe) sounded best.
translation.trainingStudio.train.artistTokenInfo: Name of the learned token. Blank = the adapter's name. Becomes a key inside the adapter file.
translation.trainingStudio.train.artistTokenKInfo: How many embedding vectors the token spans. More = more capacity; 32 measured best so far.
translation.trainingStudio.train.artistTokenLrInfo: Learning rate for the token and prefix group, separate from the LoRA's. Always AdamW, even under Muon or Prodigy.
translation.trainingStudio.train.prefixNInfo: Prefix tuning: n trainable key/value columns per layer that every position attends to. 0 = off. Turns head-blocked attention off for the run.
translation.trainingStudio.train.rsloraInfo: Rank-stabilised scaling alpha/√r instead of alpha/r. Written to the adapter config and honoured at load.
translation.trainingStudio.train.loraPlusRatioInfo: B tensors learn at this multiple of A's learning rate (the paper's 16). 1 = off. AdamW-rule tensors only; Muon ignores it.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.layersHelp: Anything below the full depth trains only the top layers. It fits smaller cards, but whether a part-depth adapter sounds good is not yet established.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.cropAuto: Fitted automatically to free VRAM, between the minimum and maximum below.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.cropSecondsHelp: 60 s ≈ Side-Step chunk_duration; if it does not fit VRAM the trainer reduces trained depth (layers) — watch for the partial-depth warning.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.cropFramesHelp: Raw latent frames, about 25 per second. Rounded down to an even number.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.cropHelp: Each step trains on a random window of every song, about 25 frames per second. Longer windows need more VRAM.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.tMinInfo: The lower bound of the timestep window. Draws below this are re-sampled, so raising it excludes the earliest, most-structural part of the noise schedule from training.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.tMaxInfo: The upper bound of the timestep window. Draws above this are re-sampled, so lowering it excludes the latest, most-detailed part of the noise schedule from training. Must stay above Min.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.milestoneDiskHe: Each milestone is a full copy of the adapter. That was ~84 MB at rank 16 with attention only; at the current default (rank 128, MLP projections included) it is well over a gigabyte each, so six of them can run to several GB. Lower the count, the rank, or the milestone step if disk is tight.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.mirrorHelp: Training keeps a copy of every frozen weight in a trainable layer, and that copy has two separate costs: what it takes up, and what it rounds. The default keeps the copy in the base model's own BF16 — half the VRAM, so a longer crop or more trained layers on the same card — but does the maths in F32, which matches the old F32 path number for number. Plain BF16 does the maths in BF16 too: fastest, and the one that made renders sound coarse. F32 is the original, and costs about 8 GB more. NVIDIA/CUDA only; other backends fall back to F32.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.batchHelp: Crops per micro-batch, drawn from that many different songs. Effective samples per optimizer step is batch × grad-accum steps. Default 1 (off): batching speeds up shallow / partial-depth runs (~2.4× faster per crop at 8 layers) but is typically SLOWER at full depth on a large GPU (~2.5× slower on a 32 GB card) — measured 2026-07-29.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.ckptSegmentsHel: Gradient checkpointing trades a little extra compute for a lot less VRAM by recomputing activations in segments instead of keeping them all. Auto lets the VRAM fit pick the segment count; Off uses the original single-pass graph.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.stopEngine: Stop the engine during the job
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.noBinary: ace-train was not found next to ace-server. Rebuild the engine to enable DiT training.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.needsPreprocess: This dataset has no preprocessed tensors. Run Preprocess first.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.otherJobRunning: Another job is running for this dataset. DiT training can start once it finishes.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.visibleNow: This adapter is already available in the Adapters dropdown — no restart needed.
translation.trainingStudio.train.baseSizeInfo: Which Qwen3 planner the LoRA is trained against. The adapter is bound to that base — a 4B adapter will not load on a 0.6B planner — so this is the one choice you cannot revise later. 0.6B and 1.7B train on the standard path; 4B switches to low-VRAM mode (per-layer gradient checkpointing plus a chunked loss head), needs around 12 GB, and is slower per step. 4B is what gets used here in practice; 0.6B is the safe-on-any-card option.
translation.trainingStudio.train.adapterNameInfo: Folder name for the finished adapter. Letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores, up to 64 characters, not starting with a dot. It lands in lm-<size>/<name>/<timestamp>/, so training the same name twice never overwrites the earlier run — you get a second timestamped folder beside it.
translation.trainingStudio.train.targetLossInfo: The real stopping condition: the run ends the moment an epoch's average loss reaches this, and Max epochs is only the backstop. LM loss is cross-entropy over 5 Hz code tokens and sits on its own scale, separate from DiT loss — the default here is 0.1. Lower fits your dataset harder and eventually memorises it; higher stops early and leaves the adapter weak. 0 disables the auto-stop and always runs to the epoch cap.
translation.trainingStudio.train.maxEpochsInfo: Hard cap on passes over the dataset, reached only if the target loss never is. Raising it costs time rather than quality — the run still stops at the target when it gets there. Lower it when you want a guaranteed wall-clock bound. A real 4B run typically auto-stops around epoch 30.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lmModelInfo: Which installed LM file to train against, when more than one of the selected size exists. Leave it on the default unless you have a specific reason. The file must genuinely be the size selected above: a mismatch is only caught after the engine has been stopped and ace-train has read the weights, so it fails late and noisily. The bf16 projection-weights setting additionally requires a BF16-quantized base.
translation.trainingStudio.train.rankInfo: Width of the low-rank update — how much capacity the adapter has. Higher ranks can encode more of your dataset's structure, at a proportionally larger file and slower step; lower ranks generalise more and can underfit. 16 is plenty for teaching the planner one artist's section layout and phrasing. Change alpha alongside it: applied strength is alpha ÷ rank.
translation.trainingStudio.train.alphaInfo: Scales the trained update when it is applied — the adapter contributes alpha ÷ rank of what it learned, so the default 32/16 pair is 2×. Raising alpha alone makes the adapter act stronger without giving it more capacity, which tends to read as stiff, over-committed planning; lowering it makes it subtler. Keep the ratio in view whenever you change rank.
translation.trainingStudio.train.learningRateInfo: Step size for each optimizer update. 1e-4 is the validated LM default. Too high shows up as a loss curve that spikes or plateaus high; too low and the run crawls and hits the epoch cap without ever reaching the target. Change it by factors of two or three, not small nudges — anything less is lost in run-to-run noise.
translation.trainingStudio.train.gradAccumInfo: How many samples are accumulated before one optimizer step — the effective batch size. Higher gives smoother, less noisy gradients and fewer, larger steps per epoch; lower gives noisier updates, which acts as a mild regulariser. Since micro-batching is not built for the LM, this is the only way to change batch size here.
translation.trainingStudio.train.gradClipInfo: Caps the global gradient norm before each optimizer step, so one pathological sample cannot blow up the weights. 1.0 is the standard value and is applied in-graph. 0 disables clipping entirely — worth trying only if you suspect clipping is flattening real signal, and expect loss spikes if you do.
translation.trainingStudio.train.warmupRatioInfo: Fraction of the whole run spent ramping the learning rate up from zero before the cosine decay starts. It stops the first and largest steps being taken on a freshly-initialised adapter. Raise it if you are pushing the learning rate; lower it on very short runs, where 5% is only an epoch or two and the ramp never finishes.
translation.trainingStudio.train.weightDecayInfo: AdamW's pull of the trained weights back towards zero on every step — the main regulariser against overfitting a small dataset. Higher keeps the adapter conservative and close to the base model; 0 removes the pull and lets it commit fully to your data.
translation.trainingStudio.train.maxLenInfo: Longest token sequence a training sample may be, which sets the VRAM ceiling for the whole run. 0 fits it automatically to free VRAM and is the recommended setting. Songs that tokenise longer than the limit are skipped — the panel reports how many — and pinning a larger value than actually fits will OOM rather than degrade.
translation.trainingStudio.train.weightsInfo: Precision of the frozen projection weights during the backward pass. f32-window is the shipped, validated path. bf16 is measurably faster (1.26× at 4B) and about 100 MB lighter, but its gradient-parity checks come in over their own limits, so a bf16 run is a genuinely different train rather than a faster identical one. It needs a BF16 base and low-VRAM mode, and it cannot be combined with the mm backward GEMM below.
translation.trainingStudio.train.bwdInfo: How the activation gradient is computed. Both options compute the same quantity, so this is a speed lever rather than a quality trade — but for the LM, leave it on outprod. The bf16 projection-weights setting already reaches the fast mul_mat backward by a different internal route, and the two collide: the pair is refused with an error instead of being silently ignored. Choosing mm here means also dropping projection weights back to f32-window, which gives up more than mm wins.
translation.trainingStudio.train.batchInfo: Samples per forward/backward pass. Fixed at 1 — micro-batching was measured before being written and did not clear its own bar. It cannot make the maths cheaper; it only spreads per-step host overhead across samples, and that overhead is 9.3% of a step at 4B against a 10% requirement, some of which padding waste would eat back. Use gradient accumulation to change the effective batch size instead.
translation.trainingStudio.train.seedInfo: Seeds every random choice in the run — sample order, dropout, noise. The same seed with the same settings and dataset reproduces the same adapter. Change it to get a genuinely different run from identical settings, which is the honest way to tell a real improvement from a lucky draw.
translation.trainingStudio.train.orderInfo: How songs are ordered within each epoch. shuffle re-randomises every epoch, which is what you want — it stops the adapter learning the running order along with the material. fixed walks them in dataset order every time, and exists for debugging and A/B comparisons where the draw sequence has to be identical between runs.
translation.trainingStudio.train.milestoneStepInfo: Saves a full copy of the adapter every time the loss drops by this much, so you can return to an earlier, less-overfitted version after listening. LM loss lives on a large scale, so 1.0 is the sensible step here. 0 turns milestones off and keeps only the final adapter.
translation.trainingStudio.train.milestoneKeepInfo: How many milestone copies to keep on disk; the oldest is deleted as new ones arrive. Each one is a complete adapter, so this is a straight disk trade against how far back you can rewind.
translation.trainingStudio.train.stagesInfo: Which parts of the pipeline this job runs. extract encodes every song to 5 Hz codes (songs already cached are skipped), train runs the optimisation, export writes the PEFT adapter directory the app can load. Unticking a stage is for resuming or debugging — a normal run wants all three.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lossOnCotInfo: Whether the reasoning block the planner emits before its codes contributes to the loss. On, the adapter learns your dataset's planning style as well as its output. Off, only the final codes are trained on and the reasoning stays purely the base model's.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.resumeFromLates: Continues training from the newest existing run of this adapter name instead of starting from scratch, paying only for the new epochs. The adapter's identity (type, rank/dims, MLP targeting, layer window) is adopted from that run's own log — a lower target loss is the usual reason to resume. Calibrated bakes are skipped as sources; the resumed run gets its own fresh folder, so nothing is overwritten. On an adapter name that has never been trained there is nothing to continue from, and the run simply starts from scratch.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.calibrateInfo: After training, renders this dataset's songs through the base DiT, the previous adapter and the new one — conditioned on each song's own real audio codes, so only the sound differs — and measures which lands closest to the dataset's real audio in latent space (at more than one adapter scale, including below 1.0). The winner ships with its optimal scale baked in and its score saved with the adapter. If the new adapter does not measurably beat the previous one, the previous one is kept — a training run can never silently make an artist sound worse.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.calibrateRepoin: Lets the calibration step update this artist's album preset(s) to point at whichever adapter won. With this off the winner is still baked and scored, but presets keep playing whatever they pointed at before.
translation.trainingStudio.train.resumeFromLatestInf: Continues training from the newest existing run of this adapter name instead of starting from scratch, paying only for the new epochs. The adapter's identity (type, rank, LoKR dims, precision mode) is adopted from that run's own log — a lower target loss is the usual reason to resume. Calibrated bakes are skipped as sources; the resumed run gets its own fresh folder, so nothing is overwritten. On an adapter name that has never been trained there is nothing to continue from, and the run simply starts from scratch.
translation.trainingStudio.train.calibrateInfo: After training, generates plans with the base LM, the previous adapter and the new one on this dataset's own captions, measures which lands closest to the dataset's real audio codes (at more than one adapter scale, including below 1.0), and ships the winner with its optimal scale baked in. The winner's score is saved with the adapter and shown in the adapter pickers. If the new adapter does not measurably beat the previous one, the previous one is kept — a training run can never silently make an artist worse.
translation.trainingStudio.train.captionDropoutInfo: Trains some fraction of style steps with the caption dropped, so the adapter learns to plan from the artist's own code statistics instead of leaning entirely on the caption text. Ported from the MiniMax-Music3 LM trainer's equivalent lever. Default 30% since 2026-09-03: combined with prior preservation it measured best on loudness and timbre in a 3-artist render-scored experiment (on its own it hurt, so keep prior preservation on with it). Not yet validated by ear. 0% reproduces the pre-lever run exactly; needs a trigger word on the dataset.
translation.trainingStudio.train.priorPreservationIn: Spends some steps on an automatically-picked UNRELATED artist's dataset, scored against what the base model itself predicted there rather than against that artist's music. The adapter is then penalised for changing its mind about material that has nothing to do with THIS artist — the only term in the objective that separates "learned the voice" from "rewrote the planner". Ported from the MiniMax-Music3 LM trainer's equivalent lever. Off by default since 2026-09-04, when the default recipe became the one picked by ear, which trains without it. Turned on, it runs every 3rd step. In a 3-artist render-scored experiment it produced the fewest looping plans and moved loudness and timbre closest to the artist. Not yet validated by ear. Needs at least one other artist preprocessed at 600 s; the server refuses the run when none exists.
translation.trainingStudio.train.regEveryInfo: Cadence of prior-preservation steps: 3 means one regularisation step per two style steps. Must be at least 2 — at 1 every step would regularise and nothing would learn the artist.
translation.trainingStudio.train.regTopkInfo: Classes kept per position in the captured prior distributions. Higher covers more of the base model's probability mass at the cost of a larger cache.
translation.trainingStudio.train.regTeacherInfo: What the regularisation step is scored against. Cached (default) captures a top-K slice of the base model's predictions once per corpus and reuses it — fast, but covers only a fraction of the base's probability mass. Live instead runs the frozen base fresh on every regularisation step and scores against its full distribution over the audio-code vocabulary — 100% coverage, no cache, at the cost of an extra forward pass per regularisation step. New (2026-09-03) and unvalidated by ear.
translation.trainingStudio.train.calibrateRepointInf: Lets the calibration step update this artist's album preset(s) to point at whichever adapter won. With this off the winner is still baked and scored, but presets keep playing whatever they pointed at before.
translation.trainingStudio.train.reextractInfo: Re-encodes every song's 5 Hz codes from scratch instead of reusing the cache. Only needed when the audio or captions changed underneath an existing cache — it adds the full extraction pass to the front of the job.
translation.trainingStudio.train.stopEngineInfo: Shuts ace-server down for the duration of the job and restarts it afterwards, so the trainer gets the whole GPU. Leave it on: training and a loaded inference engine compete for the same VRAM, and the run's whole memory fit is calculated from what is free when it starts. Turning it off keeps music generation available but risks an OOM, or a much smaller configuration than the card could really carry.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.adapterTypeInfo: LoKR factors the update as a Kronecker product instead of a plain low-rank product, reaching comparable quality with far fewer trained parameters — smaller files, faster steps. It is the recommended default. LoRA is the classic form and the one every external tool understands first. Switching type resets the whole form to that type's defaults, because the two genuinely need different learning rates and loss settings; only the adapter name is carried over.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.baseModelInfo: The DiT this adapter attaches to. It is fixed rather than chosen: the cached latents, context latents and encoder states in this preprocess variant are this exact model's own output, so training them against a different base would be meaningless. To train another base, preprocess the dataset again against it.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.qualityInfo: A preset dial over four fields at once — epoch cap, window maximum, milestone step and target loss. Fast is a quick shape check (100 epochs, shorter windows), Balanced is the normal run (400), Thorough runs 800 epochs to a lower target for a dataset you are committed to. Every field stays individually editable afterwards; clicking a preset again resets those four.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.adapterNameInfo: Folder name for the finished adapter. Letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores, up to 64 characters, not starting with a dot. It lands in dit-<base>/<name>/<timestamp>/, so re-training under the same name adds a new timestamped run rather than overwriting the old one.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.targetLossInfo: The real stopping condition: the run ends when the 5-epoch moving average of the loss reaches this. DiT loss is a rectified-flow velocity error on its own scale, separate from LM loss — the default here is 0.1, deliberately ambitious: the run always keeps its best adapter, so an unreached target costs nothing and simply means the whole epoch horizon is used. Short runs will not reach it at all and stop at the epoch cap instead. 0 disables the auto-stop.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.maxEpochsInfo: Hard cap on passes over the dataset, reached only if the target loss never is — which for DiT is the common case, so in practice this is what decides how long a run takes. One epoch is a single random window from each song, not the whole track.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.lokrDimInfo: Upper bound on the rank of each Kronecker block — LoKR's capacity knob and the analogue of LoRA rank. 512 with factor 6 is the validated Uber-LoKR configuration. Lower it for a smaller, more general adapter; raising it grows the file and the step cost without necessarily learning more, because the factorisation rather than this number is usually the binding constraint.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.lokrAlphaInfo: Scales the applied LoKR update the way alpha does for LoRA — effective strength is alpha ÷ dim, so the default 512/512 pair is 1×. Keeping them equal matters more than it sounds: an alpha well below dim silently weakens whole blocks, which is exactly how an earlier preset ended up merging its MLP sites at a quarter strength. Move it only when you know why.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.lokrFactorInfo: How each weight matrix is split into the two Kronecker factors. A larger factor makes one factor wide and the other narrow, changing both the parameter count and which shapes the adapter can express. 6 is the validated default; -1 lets the factorisation pick the most balanced split it can find. Must be -1, or between 2 and 64.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.lokrDecomposeBo: Trains both Kronecker factors instead of only the larger one, which is what LyCORIS and Side-Step do. On gives the adapter its full expressiveness and keeps parity with those reference implementations; off trains fewer parameters and is only worth trying if you are chasing file size.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.rankInfo: Width of the low-rank update at each trained site — the adapter's capacity. The DiT default is far higher than the LM's because timbre and production carry more detail than sentence structure. Higher ranks mean a bigger file, more VRAM and a slower step, and the auto-fit will shorten the audio window to pay for it; lower ranks generalise more and can miss what makes a sound distinctive.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.alphaInfo: Scales the trained update when it is applied — the adapter contributes alpha ÷ rank of what it learned, so the default 256/128 pair is 2×. Raising alpha alone makes the adapter act stronger at generation time without adding capacity, which usually reads as harsh or over-processed; lowering it makes it subtler.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.layersInfo: How many transformer layers get an adapter, counted from the top. 0 fits it automatically to free VRAM and is the recommended setting. Anything below full depth trains only the top layers, which is how smaller cards fit at all, but whether a part-depth adapter actually sounds good is not established. Note the auto-fit deliberately shortens the audio window before it reduces depth — depth is the quality axis.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.cropInfo: Each step trains on one random window from each song rather than the whole track: full-song, full-depth training would need roughly 68 GB, because there is no flash-attention backward and the softmax has to be retained. Auto takes the longest window that fits between the minimum and maximum below, which is what you want. Pinning a length instead forces the fit to give up trained depth to keep it — watch for the partial-depth warning. Windows are latent frames, about 25 per second, rounded down to an even number.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.cropMinInfo: Shortest window the auto-fit is allowed to settle on, in latent frames (about 25 per second, so 375 ≈ 15 s). If even this does not fit, the fit starts reducing trained depth instead. Raise it to refuse windows you consider too short to carry a song's character.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.cropMaxInfo: Longest window the auto-fit will use, in latent frames (1250 ≈ 50 s). It is a ceiling, not a target — the fit takes the largest window that genuinely fits below it. The measured ceiling on a 24 GB card at full depth is roughly 1000–1250 frames.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.learningRateInf: Step size for each optimizer update, and the setting that differs most between adapter types: 5e-4 for LoRA, 2e-3 for LoKR. These are not interchangeable — 1e-4 was measured not to train the DiT at all. Too high shows as a loss curve that rises or plateaus noisily; too low as one that barely moves.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.gradAccumInfo: How many micro-batches are accumulated before one optimizer step. It counts micro-batches, not songs, so effective samples per step is batch size × this number. Higher gives smoother gradients and fewer, larger steps; lower gives noisier ones.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.gradClipInfo: Caps the global gradient norm before each optimizer step, so one pathological window cannot blow up the weights. 1.0 is the standard value. 0 disables clipping entirely — worth trying only if you suspect it is flattening real signal, and expect loss spikes if you do.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.warmupRatioInfo: Fraction of the whole run spent ramping the learning rate up from zero before the cosine decay begins. It keeps the first and largest steps off a freshly-initialised adapter. Raise it if you are pushing the learning rate; lower it on very short runs, where 5% is a handful of steps and the schedule never really gets going.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.weightDecayInfo: AdamW's pull of the trained weights back towards zero on every step — the main regulariser against overfitting a small dataset. The default differs by adapter type: 0.01 for LoRA, 0.001 for LoKR. Higher keeps the adapter closer to the base model; 0 lets it commit fully to your data.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.lossWeightingIn: How much each sampled timestep counts towards the loss. flow_snr weights by (1−t)^bias ÷ (t·(1−t)), clamped at the SNR gamma, concentrating the run on the noise levels that carry most of the signal — this is the LoRA default. none weights every timestep equally and is the validated LoKR default. The two produce different-looking curves, so never compare loss numbers across them.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.snrGammaInfo: Ceiling on the flow_snr weight. Without it, timesteps very close to 0 or 1 get an enormous weight and a handful of samples dominate the gradient. Lower clamps harder and flattens the weighting towards uniform; higher lets extreme timesteps pull more. No effect when loss weighting is none.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.tBiasInfo: The exponent in the flow_snr weight, (1−t)^bias ÷ (t·(1−t)). It tilts emphasis along the noise schedule: higher pushes weight towards low t — the clean end, where fine detail lives — and 0 leaves the plain 1/(t·(1−t)) shape. No effect when loss weighting is none.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.channelBalanceI: Weights each of the 64 latent channels by the inverse of its standard deviation across your dataset, so loud channels do not dominate the loss and quiet ones still get trained. It needs channel_stats.json in the preprocess variant — without that file the switch does nothing at all, and the panel says so. On by default, matching Side-Step.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.timestepMuInfo: Centre of the logit-normal distribution the training timestep is drawn from: t = sigmoid(mu + sigma·z). Negative values bias the draw towards low t, the cleaner end of the schedule where fine detail lives. Move it positive to spend more of the run on heavily-noised samples, which trains structure at the expense of texture.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.timestepSigmaIn: Spread of that same logit-normal draw. Larger values sample the whole noise schedule more evenly, including both extremes; smaller values concentrate the run tightly around mu. Very small values effectively train one noise level and generalise poorly across the sampler's trajectory.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.tWindowInfo: Restricts training to a slice of the noise schedule — draws outside [min, max] are re-sampled (up to 64 tries, then clamped). The full 0 → 1 range is the default. Narrowing it is how you train an interval expert: an adapter that only acts over part of the denoising trajectory, which pairs with the timestep-dependent adapter gain curves at generation time. Min must be below max.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.cfgRatioInfo: The fraction of training samples whose text conditioning is replaced by the base model's null embedding, so the adapter learns an unconditional prediction alongside the conditioned one — that is what makes CFG behave at generation time. On a base with no null_condition_emb it cannot be applied at all, and the run warns rather than pretending it did.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.genreRatioInfo: Percentage of samples conditioned on the genre-only caption instead of the full one. It teaches the adapter to respond to a short style prompt as well as a detailed one, which is what lets a trigger word work on its own. 0 turns it off and trains only on full captions.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.seedInfo: Seeds every random choice: song order, crop positions, timesteps, noise and conditioning dropout. The same seed with the same settings and dataset reproduces the same adapter exactly. Change it to get a genuinely different run from identical settings.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.orderInfo: How songs are ordered within each epoch. shuffle re-randomises every epoch, which is what you want — it stops the adapter learning the running order along with the material. fixed walks them in dataset order every time, for debugging and for A/B comparisons where the draw sequence has to match.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.milestoneStepIn: Saves a full copy of the adapter every time the loss drops by this much, so you can go back to an earlier, less-baked version after listening. Mind the disk cost — at the current rank-128-with-MLP defaults each copy is well over a gigabyte. 0 turns milestones off and keeps only the final adapter.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.milestoneKeepIn: How many milestone copies to keep; the oldest is deleted as new ones arrive. Each is a complete adapter, so six at the current defaults can run to several GB. Lower this, the rank, or the milestone step if disk is tight.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.vramReserveInfo: VRAM the fit leaves unallocated for the desktop, the browser and anything else on the card. Too low and the run competes with your display and can be killed by the driver; raising it costs window length or trained depth, because the fit only ever spends what is left after this.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.mirrorInfo: Training keeps a copy of every frozen weight in a trainable layer. BF16 keeps that copy in the base model's own precision, roughly halving its VRAM — which buys a longer window or more trained layers on the same card — and the measured loss difference against F32 is about 8e-5, i.e. rounding. F32 is the older, conservatively-validated path. NVIDIA/CUDA only: the engine falls back to F32 with a warning on any other backend.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.bwdInfo: How the activation gradient is computed. Both options compute exactly the same quantity — this is a speed lever, not a quality trade like Mirror precision. mm uses a dtype-agnostic mul_mat, so a BF16 mirror can ride BF16 tensor cores in both directions: measured 1.10–1.17× end-to-end on an RTX 5090, with loss matching to about 7e-5. outprod is upstream ggml's F32-only formulation. Leave it on mm unless you specifically suspect the fast path.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.batchInfo: Crops per micro-batch, drawn from that many different songs. Effective samples per optimizer step is this × gradient accumulation. Default 1 (off), on measurement: batching is about 2.5× SLOWER at full depth on a 32 GB card — that graph is already compute-bound, and batching forces checkpointing and a smaller window just to fit — but about 2.4× FASTER on shallow or partial-depth runs. Raise it only for the shallow case.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.ckptSegmentsInf: Gradient checkpointing recomputes activations in segments instead of holding them all, trading roughly 30–40% extra forward time for a large VRAM saving. Auto lets the VRAM fit choose, and resolves to a single unsegmented pass whenever full depth already fits — so Auto costs nothing when it is not needed. Off forces the original monolithic graph. A fixed count pins the segmentation: more segments means less VRAM and more recompute.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.stagesInfo: Which parts of the job run. train runs the optimisation; export writes the PEFT adapter directory the app can load. Unticking one is for debugging or resuming — a normal run wants both.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.targetMlpInfo: Adds the gate/up/down projections to the eight attention sites the adapter already covers. On by default — most of a record's timbre lives in the MLP, and this is usually the difference between an adapter that changes the mix and one that changes the sound. It costs VRAM, so the auto-fit will shorten the audio window to pay for it.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.stopEngineInfo: Shuts ace-server down for the duration of the job and restarts it afterwards, so the trainer gets the whole GPU. Leave it on: training and a loaded inference engine compete for the same VRAM, and the run's whole memory fit is calculated from what is free when it starts. Turning it off keeps music generation available but risks an OOM, or a far smaller configuration than the card could really carry.

translation.midiStudio.abc.info: Writes this transcription as the two-voice ABC score YuE2 covers use: the sung notes as the Vocal line, one instrument's top line as the Ins line, an estimated key and chord symbols, on the bars above. Paste it into Cover Studio's ABC box to skip transcription there. Drums and the other instruments are left out.

translation.midiStudio.tempoModelInfo: Beat This! (CPJKU), an 80 MB beat and downbeat tracker. With it, every new transcription gets the song's tempo, a time signature and bar lines, so the MIDI lines up with the grid in a DAW or notation app. Without it the MIDI is written at a fixed 120 BPM.
translation.midiStudio.tempoModelReady: Ready: new transcriptions get tempo and bar lines
translation.midiStudio.speculativeInfo: Faster large-model transcription. The small model guesses the next few notes and the large model checks them in one pass, keeping only what it would have written itself, so the MIDI is the same. About a third faster on a full song with a GPU. Needs the small model's weights too and uses about 0.5 GB more memory.
translation.midiStudio.speculativeNeedsSmall: Download the small model to use this; until then the large model runs on its own.
translation.midiStudio.export.title: Tempo & bars
translation.midiStudio.export.bpmInfo: Write one fixed tempo instead of the detected one. Bar lines then sit at this tempo from the first downbeat, and any tempo map is dropped.
translation.midiStudio.export.beatsPerBarInfo: The time signature's top number (the bottom is always 4). Set it when the meter came out unknown or wrong, for example 3 for a waltz or 6 for a 6/8 feel counted in quarter notes.
translation.midiStudio.export.tempoInfo: Automatic writes one tempo when the beats are steady and a tempo map when they drift. Follows the performance always writes the tempo map, which keeps bar lines on the beat through tempo changes. One tempo always writes a single tempo, which notation apps handle best.
translation.midiStudio.export.beatScaleInfo: Use when the tempo came out at half or double what you hear. Double time puts a beat between each detected pair; half time keeps every other beat.
translation.midiStudio.export.quantizeInfo: Snap note starts and ends to a grid. Notation apps need this to avoid tiny rests and odd tuplets; for playback it removes some of the feel.
translation.midiStudio.export.gridInfo: The note value to snap to. Detected uses the subdivision the notes were measured to sit on.
translation.midiStudio.export.strengthInfo: How far notes move toward the grid. 100% snaps them onto it; lower values keep some of the timing of the performance.
translation.midiStudio.export.fillGapsInfo: Hold each note until the next note of its instrument when the gap is half a beat or less, so a score shows held notes instead of short ones followed by rests.
translation.midiStudio.export.trimLeadingInfo: Drop the empty bars before the first note. The MIDI then no longer starts where the audio does.

translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.optimizerInfo: Which update rule the trainable parameters use. Muon is the default: every 2-D parameter whose short side is at least 16 gets an orthogonalised-momentum (Newton-Schulz) update, and everything else — including a LoKR w1, which is 4x5 and where orthogonalising means nothing — stays on AdamW. Muon also needs only one momentum buffer instead of two, freeing about 870 MB at LoKR dim 512. Measured over a full run it reached the target loss in 161 epochs against AdamW’s 227. AdamW remains available and unchanged if you want to compare.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.optimizerHint: Prodigy is the default: it estimates its own step size, so the learning-rate field is ignored. Muon (ear-validated in July) and AdamW remain one select away.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.muonLrScaleInfo: Multiplies the learning-rate schedule for Muon parameters ONLY. Muon's update is normalised by construction, so its learning rate does not mean what AdamW's does — per element an orthogonalised update is roughly 20x smaller, which is why the default is 20. Measured on a LoKR dim-512 run: 5 undershoots, 20 matches AdamW, 50 overshoots. Non-Muon parameters keep the plain learning rate.
translation.trainingStudio.train.dit.muonNsStepsInfo: How many Newton-Schulz iterations orthogonalise each update. Five is the reference value and pulls the singular values into a band around 1; the iteration targets that band rather than converging, so more steps buy little. Fewer steps make each optimizer step cheaper but only slightly — most of the cost is the number of separate operations, not the iteration count.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.adapterTypeInfo: How the adapter is parameterised. LoRA is the default and the long-proven path: two low-rank matrices per site. LoKr instead factorises each site as a Kronecker product, which reaches a different capacity/size trade — a dim-512 LoKr on the 0.6B is 22.0M parameters against a rank-16 LoRA’s 10.1M. The maths is gated (a zero-init LoKr perturbs nothing, and the contraction matches a materialised Kronecker product exactly), but the hyperparameters below are carried over from the DiT and have not been tuned on an LM, so treat LoKr as experimental here. A LoKr writes lokr_weights.safetensors instead of adapter_model.safetensors.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.adapterTypeHint: LoRA unless you are deliberately testing LoKr or one of the parameterizations beside it. DoRA/HiRA/LoHa/HRA/PiSSA joined the LM trainer 2026-09-05, porting train-dit's method row — none of them has an LM-specific measurement yet, only the DiT blind test linked from each button's hover text.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.doraInfo: Weight-decomposed LoRA: a learned per-output magnitude on top of the LoRA direction. Not yet run on the LM — see trainingStudio.train.dit.doraInfo for the only measurement that exists (blind test, last of five on the DiT). Exports lora_magnitude_vector.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.hiraInfo: Hadamard high-rank adaptation: the base weight modulates the LoRA update (W + W ⊙ BA), so the effective rank is not capped by r. Not yet run on the LM — on the DiT it had the lowest training loss of the set at ~1.5x the time per epoch. Merge mode only.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.lohaInfo: LyCORIS LoHa: two LoRA pairs multiplied element-wise, effective rank up to r². Not yet run on the LM — on the DiT it matched LoRA's loss trajectory at ~3x the time and twice the file. Exported in the LyCORIS hada_w* layout. Merge mode only.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.hraInfo: Householder Reflection Adaptation: the input at each site is rotated by a product of `rank` learned reflections before the frozen weight, so the update is orthogonal and the weight's spectrum is preserved. Not yet run on the LM — on the DiT it produced a very small adapter but ~4x the time per epoch and a much weaker change than a LoRA. Rank must be even. Exports as an exact rank-r LoRA.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.hotPizzaInfo: HOT-PiZZA is PiSSA with principal-subspace dropout: PiSSA whose rank-dropout mask hits the principal component itself rather than the delta: every step a random share of the base's own top-r subspace is deleted while the adapter fits the album. MM3's default method since 2026-09-06, where it beat every other method blind on one album; not yet heard on the AS1.5 LM. Train loss reads high under it, so stop on steps. Turns PiSSA on; exports the same rank-2r LoRA.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.pissaInfo: Starts A and B on the weight's own top-r singular directions and keeps the residual in the base, so training fine-tunes the principal subspace from step one. Not yet run on the LM — on the DiT it tied plain LoRA at double the file. Exports as a normal LoRA of rank 2r. Plain LoRA only; a PiSSA run cannot be resumed.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.lokrDimInfo: Inner dimension of the Kronecker factorisation. Larger means more capacity and a bigger adapter. 512 is carried over from the DiT, where it was tuned against a 2.5B model — it is not a measured value for an LM.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.lokrFactorInfo: Caps how each dimension splits into Kronecker factors: the largest divisor at or below this becomes the small side. 6 splits a 2560-wide projection into 5 x 512. Use -1 for the most balanced split available. Every projection in the model must factorise or training refuses up front rather than producing an unloadable adapter.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.optimizerInfo: Which update rule the adapter parameters use. AdamW is the default and the long-proven path. Muon instead orthogonalises the update for every 2-D parameter whose short side is at least 16 — and for a LoRA the short side is the RANK, so at rank 16 every matrix qualifies and at rank 8 none would (the run log reports the split). On the DiT Muon reached the target in 1.41x fewer epochs and was ear-validated; on the LM only a short smoke run exists, so it is unproven here. Muon also needs one momentum buffer instead of two, which frees VRAM.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.optimizerHint: AdamW is the default. Prodigy estimates its own step size, so the learning-rate field is ignored when it is picked.
translation.trainingStudio.train.lm.muonLrScaleInfo: Multiplies the learning-rate schedule for Muon parameters only. Muon’s update is normalised by construction, so its learning rate does not mean what AdamW’s does — per element it is roughly 20x smaller, which is where the default comes from. That 20 was measured on the DiT, not the LM, so it is the first knob to move if a Muon run looks wrong early.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.codesBlurb: MiniMax-Music3 ships no audio-to-code encoder, so the tokens the LM learns from are produced here, natively, by the adopted community encoder. Run this once per dataset; re-running overwrites with whichever encoder is installed now.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.trainBlurb: Trains the planner LM on this dataset. Checkpoints are written straight to the MiniMax-Music3 adapter folder, so they appear in the generation panel's adapter picker as soon as they are saved — there is no install step. The engine is paused for the run.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.needsCodes: Export the RVQ codes first — training reads them, not the audio.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.preset.fastInfo: 300 steps, every track trained as one whole song (window 360 s, no history prefix). About 30 to 60 minutes per album on a 32 GB card, depending on track length. Whole-song training is what taught adapters to keep a song's shape and end it: the 2026-09-10 overnight moved natural endings from 1 in 6 to about 1 in 2 across three albums.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.preset.balancedInfo: The default: 600 steps, every track trained as one whole song (window 360 s, no history prefix). About 1 to 2 hours per album on a 32 GB card. Same recipe as Fast with twice the depth.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.preset.thoroughInfo: 900 steps, every track trained as one whole song (window 360 s, no history prefix). About 1.5 to 3 hours per album on a 32 GB card. Three times Fast's depth; whether the extra steps buy anything by ear is not yet measured.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.preset.customInfo: Steps, learning rate, crop or history differ from every preset.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.updateLinkedPresetsHi: When the run finishes, Lyric Studio album presets linked to this dataset are pointed at its final checkpoint. Turn off for test runs so they do not replace a preset you use.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.keepResumeStateHint: The optimizer state (about 4 GB) lets a finished run be continued past its step count. Off: it is deleted once the run ends. A run that stops early keeps it either way.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.adapterTypeHint: LoRA is the default. LoKr trains a Kronecker pair per slot for a smaller file (about 528 MB at factor 6 against a rank-128 LoRA's 1.4 GB) — NOT YET VALIDATED BY EAR. DoRA/HiRA/LoHa/HRA joined this row 2026-09-05, porting train-dit's method row; none has an MM3-specific measurement of its own yet — see each button's hover text for the only measurement that exists (the DiT blind test).
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.doraInfo: Weight-decomposed LoRA: a learned per-output magnitude on top of the LoRA direction. Not yet run on MM3 — see the DiT's blind test (last of five) for the only measurement that exists. Exports lora_magnitude_vector.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.hiraInfo: Hadamard high-rank adaptation: the base weight modulates the LoRA update (W + W ⊙ BA), so the effective rank is not capped by r. Not yet run on MM3 — on the DiT it had the lowest training loss of the set at ~1.5x the time per epoch. Merge mode only.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.lohaInfo: LyCORIS LoHa: two LoRA pairs multiplied element-wise, effective rank up to r². Not yet run on MM3 — on the DiT it matched LoRA's loss trajectory at ~3x the time and twice the file. Merge mode only.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.hraInfo: Householder Reflection Adaptation: the input at each site is rotated by a product of learned reflections before the frozen weight, preserving the weight's spectrum. Not yet run on MM3 — on the DiT it produced a very small adapter but ~4x the time per epoch. Rank must be even.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.hotPizzaInfo: The default since 2026-09-06. HOT-PiZZA is PiSSA with principal-subspace dropout: PiSSA whose rank-dropout mask hits the principal component itself rather than the delta: every step a random share of the base's own top-128 subspace is deleted while the adapter fits the album. Found by accident, kept because its adapter beat every other method blind on albumA twice (LoRA next, then DoRA; LoKr and corrected PiSSA both produced drone plans). One album so far. Train loss reads high under it, so stop on steps (500 heard; 250/350 under test). Turns PiSSA on; exports an ordinary rank-2r LoRA.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.pissaInfo: Starts A and B on the weight's own top-r singular directions, keeping the residual in the base. Not yet run on MM3 — on the DiT it tied plain LoRA at double the file. Plain LoRA only; not resumable.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.rsloraInfo: Rank-stabilised scaling alpha/√r instead of alpha/r. Written to the adapter config and honoured at load. Not with HRA.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.loraPlusRatioInfo: B tensors learn at this multiple of A's learning rate (the paper's 16). 1 = off. AdamW/Prodigy-rule tensors only; Muon ignores it.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.attnBackendHelp: Fused attention kernels — see the VRAM estimate above for the measured saving.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.attnBackendHelpPendin: Fused attention kernels — the engine flag landed 2026-09-05, but the VRAM saving is not yet measured, so the estimate above stands in with exact mode's number until it is. Refused together with a nonzero History-before-crop prefix (below, on by default): a frozen prefix makes the attention mask rectangular, which the fused ops do not accept, so the server coerces this back to exact rather than let the run fail on a setting you never touched. Turn History off first if you actually want flash running.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.softPromptGroupHelp: A named token adds k learned vectors behind a placeholder in every caption; the prefix adds n trainable key/value columns per layer. Both train WITH the LoRA and ship in the same adapter file. Different mechanism from "History before crop" below, which is FROZEN real-audio context, not a trained parameter.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.prefixNInfo: n trainable key/value columns per layer that every position attends to. 0 = off. Not the frozen history prefix below — this one trains.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.prefixNVsReg: Unavailable with a regularisation dataset: the prior capture needs an inert model, and a prefix is non-zero from initialisation. The engine refuses the pair.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.previewSongHint: Rows marked "likely instrumental" are exactly what the auto-pick now avoids — pick one anyway if that is deliberately what you want to hear.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.previewSongDisabled: Ignored while the caption box below is filled in.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.triggerHint: Recorded in the adapter sidecar so the picker can show it. Your captions should already contain it — this does not add it to them.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.optimizerHint: Muon is the default for two reasons: at rank 256 AdamW's second momentum buffer does not fit on a 32 GB card, and Muon's normalised update means an AdamW learning rate does not apply to it.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.muonLrScaleHint: 64 is the best of the values measured so far, not a tuned optimum.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.cropModeHint: `beginning` trains on song intros only — it exists to reproduce a known failure, not to be used. Leave this on random.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.phaseCodesSub: Audio → RVQ codes, the MiniMax-Music3 equivalent of preprocessing
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.notTensors: This replaces the ACE-Step tensor cache: the two pipelines share nothing, and an ACE variant can never be used by a MiniMax-Music3 run.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.enginePaused: The engine is paused while this runs and restarted afterwards.
translation.trainingStudio.backendHint: Training follows the active generation backend. Switch it with the engine picker at the top of the sidebar.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.peakFits: Estimated peak {{gb}} GB of {{totalGb}} GB — fits with room to spare.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.peakTight: Estimated peak {{gb}} GB of {{totalGb}} GB — fits, but with almost nothing spare. Anything else using the GPU will push this into shared memory and steps will take 3–4x longer. Close other GPU apps, or drop the rank.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.peakOver: Estimated peak {{gb}} GB exceeds your {{totalGb}} GB card. Pick a smaller base, or lower the LoRA rank — rank is the largest term after the base itself.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.peakNoFit: Estimated peak {{gb}} GB against a {{totalGb}} GB card, and no combination of base and rank in this catalogue fits it. MiniMax-Music3 LM training needs roughly 11 GB at the smallest usable settings. You can still train ACE-Step 1.5 adapters, which are far smaller.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.peakUnknown: Estimated peak {{gb}} GB. Card size unknown (the engine is not running), so this is not checked against your GPU.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.baseHint: Every base trains the same way — the frozen weights are dequantized in-graph, so only VRAM and fidelity change, and step time barely moves (within ~5% across the whole range). Pick the smallest one that comfortably fits your card, then spend what is left on LoRA rank.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.basePoor: This base is too lossy to train against: measured +14% on the first-step loss and roughly double the gradient norm, i.e. the quantizer injects more error than the adapter is being asked to learn. Prefer the smallest base marked good or better that fits.
translation.trainingStudio.mm3.holdoutHint: 0 disables evaluation — the training loss then cannot tell learning from memorising. Ignored below 6 songs.

translation.settings.dataFolder.restartFailed: Restart failed. Restart the app to continue.
translation.settings.dataFolder.actionInfo: Choose whether to move your current data, use another existing library, start an empty library, or import a previous install.
translation.settings.dataFolder.moveInfo: Moves managed data into an empty destination. Across drives, verifies the copy before removing the source. External paths stay in place.
translation.settings.dataFolder.repointInfo: Opens an existing compatible data folder. Copies and deletes nothing, and does not merge libraries.
translation.settings.dataFolder.createInfo: Starts a new empty library at the destination. Your current data stays in its original folder.
translation.settings.dataFolder.importInfo: Moves the library, models, adapters, logs, Whisper models and settings from a previous app install into this data folder, and copies the Lua plugins and runtime libraries it has that this app does not ship. The old app folder stays, without that data. Import only fills an empty library; libraries are never merged.
translation.settings.dataFolder.targetInfo: Enter a full absolute folder path. For import, choose the previous app install, not its data subfolder.
translation.settings.report.title: Report an issue
translation.settings.report.intro: Describe the problem, check the exact text below, then send it to GitHub. It opens in your browser and you submit it from your own GitHub account. Nothing is sent from here.
translation.settings.report.titleInfo: A short summary of the problem.
translation.settings.report.descriptionInfo: What you did, what you expected and what you saw instead.
translation.settings.report.previewLabel: Exact text that will be sent
translation.settings.report.previewInfo: Logs have your home folder, user name, IP addresses and anything that looks like a key or token masked. Read it before you send.
translation.settings.report.trimmed: The log tail was shortened to fit the link. Use Copy full logs to paste or attach the rest.
translation.settings.updates.title: Updates
translation.settings.updates.installedInfo: The release tag or source commit this copy was built from, and the build variant. Read from the build record shipped with the app.
translation.settings.updates.channelInfo: Which feed Check now compares against. Release looks at the latest published release; Master looks at the newest commit on master. This only changes what is checked, never your installation.
translation.settings.updates.throttled: Checked less than a minute ago, so the saved result is shown.
translation.settings.updates.retryAfter: GitHub asked us to wait. Next check after {{time}}.
translation.settings.updates.ahead: This build is newer than the latest published one.
translation.settings.updates.noInstall: Download it from GitHub and install it yourself; the app does not update itself yet.
translation.settings.updates.dirty: This source checkout has uncommitted changes, so it is not compared with the feed. Commit or stash them, then check again.
translation.settings.updates.unknownIdentity: This copy has no build record (an older release, or a source folder without git), so we can't tell which version it is. Compare with the latest release on GitHub by hand.
translation.settings.updates.couldNotCheck: Could not check for updates. {{error}} This is not the same as being up to date.
translation.settings.updates.cannotCompare: The latest version was found, but it can't be compared with this build. See the link for what is current.
translation.compare.name: Name
translation.compare.nameInfo: Shown in the session list. Leave blank to use the date.
translation.compare.groupInfo: Sessions with the same group are listed together, for example one group per A/B experiment.
translation.compare.searchPlaceholder: Search the library by title or style
translation.compare.showArchivedInfo: A session archives itself once every take has a score. Turn this on to list those too.
translation.compare.empty: No comparisons yet. Start one, or select songs in the Library and press Compare.
translation.compare.deleteConfirm: Delete this comparison and its scores? Songs stay in the library.
translation.compare.levelMatchInfo: Turns every take down to the loudness of the quietest one, so you judge tone and character instead of volume. Louder nearly always sounds better at first, so leave this on for fair scoring.
translation.compare.keysHint: Space play/pause, 1-9 switch take, B or Tab A/B switch, drag a waveform to set a loop
translation.compare.abSwitchInfo: Switch between the takes in slot A and slot B at the same playhead (B or Tab). Use Set A / Set B on a take to choose them.
translation.compare.setSlotInfo: Put this take in the A/B quick switch slot
translation.compare.abSlotInfo: Slot in the A/B quick switch
translation.compare.removeTakeConfirm: Remove this take from the comparison?
translation.compare.tpInfo: True peak. Red above 0 dBTP: likely to clip after conversion.
translation.compare.diffInfo: Active take against the baseline over time. Pink: loudness difference in LU (centre line is equal). Blue: log-spectral distance in dB, higher means the tone differs more. Flat lines mean the takes sound alike there.
translation.compare.diffPickOther: Pick a take other than the baseline to see the trace

translation.hotkeys.note: Shortcuts are off while typing in a field, while a dialog is open, and in Compare studio.
translation.hotkeys.actions.focusPrev: Move the focused library row up / down
translation.hotkeys.actions.focusNext: Move the focused library row down
